title: [BE] A run never moves to another plan or a free model unless the owner names it
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. When the first paid plan's ceiling would be breached, no run is admitted on another paid plan or on a free model; it is held with the reason `budget`.
2. A ticket that names its models (a `model:` label, the existing override) is admitted on them as today, free models included. Naming a model is how the owner picks one. *Updated (2026-11-03):* a ticket naming a free model is judged on the free budget at $0 provider cost, not held by the paid ceiling; a private repository's ticket naming a free model is admitted only when the owner has opted that plan in for private repositories (`runner plan-optin -private`), and an unreadable opt-in holds it.
3. When the ceiling first binds, the owner is told once, through the existing notice, naming the plan ~~, when its window resets,~~ and the choices: wait, or name one of the listed free models on a ticket. *Updated (2026-11-03):* the notice names the window that binds and gives no reset time, since windows roll and differ by provider.
4. Plans after the first in `paid_plans` are choices ~~the owner can move first in the providers view~~; no run is admitted on one while it is not first. *Updated (2026-11-03):* the surface has no write for the plan order, so the owner chooses a plan by configuration: the `paid_plans` order and the default models change together in one PR.
5. A run stopped mid-run on `allowance-exhausted` stays stopped (negative).
6. With no ceiling binding, admission is unchanged (negative).

title: [BE] A stopped run whose ticket is closed leaves the inbox by itself
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. On each poll, the dispatcher records a ticket-closed time on every stopped run whose ticket's Linear state type is completed or canceled, read from the issues the poll already fetches.
2. The inbox drops a run with that time, as it drops an owner-cancelled run; the owner's cancel time is not written, so "cancelled by the owner" and "ticket closed elsewhere" stay distinct.
3. A stopped run whose ticket is still open is unchanged and keeps its RETRY.
4. A run marked on an earlier poll is not written again.
5. Tests cover a stopped run on a completed ticket, on a canceled ticket, on an open ticket, and an already marked run.
6. The dispatcher is deployed and, after one poll, a stopped run on a closed ticket is gone from the inbox while FRG-72's stopped run (open ticket) stays.
7. Requeueing a run clears its ticket-closed time, so a reopened ticket's retried run shows in the inbox again if it stops.

Added (2026-11-03): criterion 7, a guard added in review (a requeue clears the mark, as it clears the cancel fields).

Updated (2026-11-03): the ten stale stopped runs were cancelled by hand before this shipped, so criterion 6's live check shows the poll running cleanly with FRG-72 kept; the removal itself is proven by the store tests against the emulator.

title: [INFRA] The surface deploys itself when a merge to main changes it
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A push to `main` that changes `cmd/surface`, `web`, `internal`, the Dockerfile, `go.mod` or `go.sum` builds the surface image for linux/amd64, pushes it tagged with the commit sha and applies it to `forge-wingman-surface`; a push that changes none of them does nothing.
2. The apply is a targeted `tofu apply` of the surface service with the digest the build produced, never an untargeted apply (which resets the dispatcher's settings), so the next plan with that digest reads no changes.
3. The workflow signs in with GitHub OIDC to a deploy-only service account bound to this workflow file on `main`, with no stored key; the account can push to the surface image path, update the surface service, read the resources the targeted apply refreshes, and read and write the tofu state in `forge-wingman-tfstate` (which holds no secret values), and nothing else; it holds no grant on the dispatcher, the webhook, the database or any secret beyond what updating the service needs.
4. After the apply the job reads the service's latest revision back and fails unless it is Ready and serving the new digest; a failed deploy leaves the previous revision serving.
5. Two merges close together deploy the later commit last: runs queue, never cancel mid-apply, and an older commit never overwrites a newer image.
6. ~~The registry keeps at least the newest 20 surface images.~~ A cleanup policy keeps the newest 20 surface images and deletes older ones, and runs as a dry run before it is switched on.
7. The dispatcher and the webhook are not deployed by this workflow.
8. The apply passes the service's runtime settings (`dispatcher_settings`) from a file committed under `infra`, and the job fails unless the plan changes only the service's image; a plan that removes or changes a setting stops the deploy.
9. The workflow can also be run by hand on `main` to deploy `main` as it stands (for a merge that changed none of the paths in criterion 1); a run from any other branch stops before signing in.

Updated (2026-11-02): criterion 6 now includes a delete rule, because a keep rule only sets a minimum and deletes nothing by itself (Artifact Registry's cleanup policy documentation); the keep rule wins where both match.

Updated (2026-11-02): added criterion 8. The live surface and dispatcher carry three settings (the review limit, two-stage and the decision timeout) that exist only on the running services, so a plan run without them proposes removing them from the surface and the Configuration page would show the default review limit. Nothing in the repo records the values today, so a workflow has no source for them.

Updated (2026-11-03): criterion 3 now allows the tofu state bucket, because criterion 2's targeted apply reads and writes the shared state file; the bucket holds no secret values (secrets are created empty and filled by hand).

Added (2026-11-03): criterion 9, the manual run, so `main` can be deployed through this workflow when its last merge changed none of the surface's paths, including the first deploy after this ticket merges.

 3. A phase figure that was not recorded (a run before the per-phase split) draws "-", and a phase the run had no stage for draws "none"; both are dim. Each such cell keeps its full words as its accessible name: "not recorded", "no plan stage" or "no build stage" (an `aria-label` or visually hidden text).
 4. "Whole run" shows every run's whole-run share, a whole percent rounding half to even as the server's strings do (0.625 prints 62%).
 5. "Finished (AEST/AEDT)" reads like "30 Oct 2026, 11:42": the day with no leading zero, a three-letter month, the year, a comma, 24-hour time, on the fixed Australia/Sydney clock, from `settled_at`; a missing or unreadable value reads "not recorded". The format comes from `sydneyDateTime` in `web/src/sydney-date-time.ts`, so the Autonomy table's "Date Finished (AEST/AEDT)" column reads "17 Oct 2026, 09:12" in the same format and its tests are updated. Updated (2026-11-02): no test exists for that column today, so the date helper gets its own test.
 6. The definition line under the card title reads exactly "Build and plan are the share of that phase's opening call that came from cache, - where it was not recorded, none where the run had no such stage; whole run is every call in the run." Updated (2026-11-02): the page's existing sentence "Runs from all projects." when a project is chosen stays, as its own line under the definition.
 7. One pager for every run. The line "N older runs recorded no cache split ...", its "Show older runs" / "Hide older runs" control and the second table are removed; older runs are rows of the one table. The pager sits ABOVE the rows, directly under the definition line: "Runs 1-10 of 37", PREVIOUS and NEXT, ten a page from 768 and five below, none when everything fits, and back to page 1 whenever the project filter changes, including a return to a project the pages were once chosen under.

title: [FE] The Overview's refresh control is an icon button
body:
## Acceptance criteria

title: [FE] The pages show the rewrite rate as a guide
body:
## Acceptance criteria

The figures below are samples: the page prints the endpoint's `rate_value` and `window`, and the guide is the endpoint's `limit`.

 1. The status word is `Auto-merge is on` when `effective` is true and `Auto-merge is off` when it is false. The state called held is gone, its word `Auto-merge is held` included.
 2. With the switch on and `rate_allows` true, the rate line reads `Recommended: rewrite rate over the trailing 10 PRs is 9.8%; guide 10%`.
 3. With the switch on and the rate above the bar, the status is on and the rate line reads `on: rewrite rate over the trailing 10 PRs is 15.3%, above the 10% guide`.
 4. With the switch off and `rate_allows` true, the rate line reads `off: switched off by you; the rewrite rate is within the 10% guide`.
 5. With the switch off and the rate above the bar, it reads `off: switched off by you; rewrite rate over the trailing 10 PRs is 15.3%, above the 10% guide`.
 6. The rule bullets read `Merges itself: size S and M PRs while auto-merge is on.` and `You merge: front-end changes, size L and sampled PRs.`
 7. The Configuration page's Auto-merge row reads `Size S and M PRs merge themselves.` with the rate line of criteria 2 to 5 below it as a separate line, and its other sentence for the switch off, `Every PR waits for you to merge it.`, is unchanged.
 8. The rewrite-rate chart's reference line is labelled `10%: the guide`, and the data table's key reads `red = above the 10% guide`.
 9. No string on the Autonomy or Configuration page says the rate holds, limits, allows or turns auto-merge off or on. `reasonText` keeps a sentence for each reason token the endpoint can serve (`too-few-measured`, `no-agent-lines`, `reverted`, `evidence-unread` and the rest), worded as information about the rate, none of them as a reason auto-merge is off while the switch is on. Added (2026-11-01): no string on the Autonomy page calls the rate a gate: the by-repo note, the trend aside and the card line say "rate", and the too-few-measured token prints its own sentence, not a partial-window figure.
10. Checks: `bun run lint`, `bun run fmt:check` and `bun run build` in `web/` pass, and each of the states in criteria 1 to 5 is shown in a production build against a stubbed `/api/autonomy`.

title: [BE] The switch alone decides whether auto-merge is on
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. With the switch on and readable, `pr-meta` marks an eligible PR for auto-merge whatever the trailing rate, however few PRs are measured, whether or not they carry agent lines, and whether or not an auto-merged PR of the window was reverted. Eligibility (size S and M, the front-end hold, the 20% sample) is unchanged.
2. With the switch off, or unreadable, auto-merge stays off, with the reasons `switch-off` and `switch-unread` as today.
3. Evidence that cannot be read no longer holds auto-merge off when the switch is on. It is logged as it is now.
4. `/api/autonomy` serves `auto_merge.effective` as the switch on and readable, and nothing else. `rate_allows`, `rate_value`, `limit`, `window` and `reason` keep their names and meaning, so the page can still word the rate: `rate_allows` is whether the rate is within the bar, and `reason` is the switch's reason where the switch holds auto-merge off, else the rate's own reason, including `rate-above-bar`, `too-few-measured`, `no-agent-lines` and `reverted`.
5. The doc comments on `AutoMergeDecision`, `AutoMergeOn`, `autoMergeState.Effective` and `autoMergeState.Reason` say what they now mean, and no comment in those files says the rate gates auto-merge.
6. Tests with literal expected values: switch on with a rate of 15.3% is on; switch on with fewer than ten measured PRs is on; switch on with no agent lines is on; switch on with a reverted auto-merge in the window is on; switch on with unreadable evidence is on; switch off with a good rate is off; switch unreadable is off; the endpoint's `effective` for each of these, with `rate_allows` and `reason` unchanged from today's values.

title: [FE] The Overview re-reads on focus and has a REFRESH control
body:
## Acceptance criteria

Same harness and bands as the other Overview tickets: 1280, 1024, 768, 440 and 320.

1. **The strip.** One strip above both columns, right-aligned: "updated 2m ago" in the muted 12px text, then a REFRESH outlined pill with a 44px target. On a phone it sits under the header, above Running now.
2. **The clock.** It reads "updated just now" under a minute, then "updated 1m ago" to "updated 59m ago", "updated 1h ago" to "updated 23h ago", and "updated 1d ago" and up, with `web/src/ago.ts`'s own words. It is computed when drawn and never ticks; any re-read redraws it.
3. **Re-read on focus.** When the tab becomes visible or the window regains focus and the last read is more than 30 seconds old, the page re-reads the inbox, the projects and, once it exists, the runs in flight, in place: the old rows stay on screen and no loading panel shows. REFRESH does the same at any age.
4. **Refreshing.** While any of those reads is open the control reads "REFRESHING...", is `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled` so keyboard focus stays on it, and the strip is `aria-busy`. The clock keeps the age of the read still on screen.
5. **A failed re-read.** The strip shows "The page could not be refreshed; showing the read from 6m ago." (the age as in AC2) in the defer colour as a status, REFRESH stays available, and the old rows stay. The Projects card's own stale line is not printed a second time on the Overview.
6. **First load.** Before the first read lands the strip draws nothing and holds its 44px band, so nothing moves when it appears.

title: [INFRA] The run workflow captures and publishes screenshots
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The `shots` job runs only when the diff touches the front-end paths, and a failed capture leaves the run and the PR as they are today.
2. The evidence step and the cleanup write only under `pr-<n>/` of `evidence`, and nothing else on the branch.

4. The capture tool writes each shot as `<width>/<route>.png` (widths s, m, l, xl), the layout the runner's evidence step reads (`internal/runner/evidence.go`, which rejects any PNG outside a width folder).

Added (2026-11-03): criterion 4. The capture tool wrote `<route>-<width>.png` while the runner reads `<width>/<route>.png`, so wiring them together as written would fail every front-end run's evidence step.

Superseded (2026-11-03): ~~criterion 3 needs a live front-end run, and the runner is paused until model credits are topped up; this ticket merges with criterion 3 pending and closes when a live run proves it.~~ Criterion 3's live check moved to FRG-278 in Phase 5, with a live retry with a note, so Phase 4 can close; this ticket is Done on criteria 1, 2 and 4, merged in PR 309.

title: [BE] A front-end PR's body shows its screenshots
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. When the diff touches the front-end paths and a `shots` artifact exists, after the PR is created the `pr` step pushes the PNGs to the `evidence` branch under `pr-<n>/` and edits the PR body: a section headed "Screenshots (fixture data)" with the head sha beside it, a table of routes by the columns s, m, l and xl, each cell a 200px image whose source is that branch's raw URL.

title: [FE] A tool captures the surface at four widths from fixture data
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `bun run shots` takes a built `web/dist` and serves it with a fixture API from `web/fixtures/`: one synthetic JSON file per `/api` route the app reads, no live data. It exits non-zero if the app reads a route the fixtures lack.
2. For each route in `--routes` (default: the routes whose page file changed since the base, else all of them) it saves a full-viewport Chromium shot at 440x763 (scale 3, mobile), 768x1024, 1024x768 and 1280x800, named `<route>-<s|m|l|xl>.png`, into `--out`.

title: [BE] The plan prompt states the decision bounds and a correction names every broken one
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `planDecisionInstruction` states each bound `decision.go` enforces: the question's byte limit, each context line's, the label's, the value's and the cost's, that each is one line, and the counts of context lines and options. It is built from the same constants the check reads, so the prompt cannot drift from the check.
2. The correction round's prompt lists every bound the decision breaks, each worded as the re-check words it, not only the first. A decision breaking two names both.
3. The re-check after the correction round is unchanged: a plan still invalid then stops once as `plan-invalid`, with the first remaining error.
4. Tests: the prompt carries each limit's value from the constants; a decision breaking a context line and a cost yields a correction prompt naming both; a decision valid on the first round still takes no correction round.

title: [BE] A review's open findings get a second fix round
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A re-check that still reports a finding, the fix round's own or a new one, starts one more fix round on the build agent's own session, only while `roundTimeout` leaves review budget (`nfr1ReviewBudget`, 25 minutes) and never beyond two fix rounds.
2. The PR body's "Pre-open review" rows say which round fixed each finding ("fixed in round 2") and which are still open after round 2.
3. A first re-check that is clean takes no second round. A stage with no budget left takes none and stops as it does today.
4. The second round's tokens count as review-stage spend, as the first's do, and are recorded as their own step with their own round number.
5. Tests: open after round 1 then fixed in round 2; open after both rounds; clean after round 1; no budget left for a second round.
6. The PR notes report the cost of the second round on the first run that takes one.

title: [BE] The build projection carries the ticket-fidelity rule

2. The build projection contains it before the protocol, which the generator's own check asserts for every listed file; the plan projection does not contain it.

4. Two runs over one stack stay byte-identical, and no other constant in the generator changes.

title: [FE] The Overview shows the runs in flight
body:
## Acceptance criteria

Same harness and bands as the other Overview tickets: 1280, 1024, 768, 440 and 320.

 1. **Placement.** The section is the first card of the Overview's left column, above Actions. Projects stays on the right at 368px and starts level with it. On a phone the order is Running now, Actions, Projects, in DOM and Tab order.
 2. **Heading.** The caption reads "RUNNING NOW", and "RUNNING NOW, FORGE-WINGMAN" with a project chosen (any chosen project's name), and the rows then drop the project name. One muted aside at the right of the heading reads "bar = % of 90m run limit" and fits one line at 440 and 320. There is no count badge.
 3. **A row.** The stage chip reads "PLANNING" or "BUILDING", in the accent so the word, not colour alone, says it; then the ticket id, the project name (under All projects only; it takes a second line when the first cannot hold it, truncating there), and the title on one line ending in an ellipsis where it does not fit. Rows are not interactive: no chevron, no link, no 44px target.
 4. **The bar.** A 6px track with an accent fill, the percent and the time on one baseline at the row's right. The time is the minutes since the entry's `claimed_at`: "28m" under an hour, "1h 16m" from an hour. The percent is those minutes over 90, rounded down and held at 100. From 80 the fill takes the defer colour, and the percent beside it is the second cue. At or past 90 minutes the bar stays full at "100%" and the time keeps counting.
 5. **Name.** Each bar's accessible name reads like "FRG-74: 76 minutes used, 84 percent of the run limit".
 6. **The list.** Longest running first, three rows, then an accent underlined 52px row "Show all 5 running" (N counted from the answer) that opens the rest in place and reads "Show fewer" while open. No row repeats "90".
 7. **The queued line.** Updated (2026-10-30): desktop only; the phone draws no queued line, to keep the first Actions row's title above the fold. One muted line under the runs, from the projects' queued and held counts narrowed to the chosen project: "4 queued" for a running project, "4 queued, 3 held until resumed" where a stopped or stopping one holds some, "3 held until resumed" where it holds only held ones, "0 queued" where none. Added (2026-11-01): desktop means the two-column layout, from the 51.25rem container width, so the line is also absent at 768.
 8. **Nothing running.** "Nothing running", or "Nothing running for parallax" with that project chosen; the queued line stays.
 9. **Loading and failure.** Loading draws three skeleton rows, marks the section `aria-busy`, and the queued slot reads "Reading the runs in flight…". A failed read shows "The runs in flight could not be read. Runs already started keep going." and an outlined TRY AGAIN, as the Phases card's does; the rest of the Overview is unaffected.
10. **The filter.** The section follows the Overview's project filter at once, as Actions does; choosing a project or All moves nothing in Actions' rows.
11. **WCAG 2.2 AA** as the page: 4.5:1 text, 3:1 for the bar against its track, reflow at 320 without sideways scroll with a 39-character project name, zoom not blocked. Added (2026-11-01): the Running now section itself holds at 320 with a 39-character project name; the 96px sideways scroll that appears there comes from the Actions empty line and the Projects card's name row, which exist on `main` before this ticket, and is FRG-259.

title: [BE] The surface serves the runs in flight
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. One entry per ledger reservation, none twice: `ticket`, `repo`, `stage`, `claimed_at` (RFC 3339) and `title`.
2. `stage` is exactly `planning` or `building`: planning for a plan-stage reservation, building for every other, as `TicketRuns` words it (`internal/store/queue.go:753-758`, `dispatcher.PhaseStagePlanning` and `PhaseStageBuilding`).
3. Entries run oldest claim first. A run whose plan has settled and waits for its build holds no reservation (`internal/dispatcher/admit.go:88-90`), so it is absent.
4. The title of each entry is the run row's `ticket_title`, written at enqueue and kept by the record the runner writes at run end; a reservation whose row has none serves an empty title. Updated (2026-10-31): ~~the claim writes the title on the run row~~ is dropped, because every row already holds a title from enqueue, so nothing is written at claim.
5. The answer carries no cost, write set or run body. The endpoint is read-only and uses the surface's existing datastore access (`infra/surface.tf:19`).
6. Tests: a ledger with a plan-stage, a build-stage and a single-stage reservation; an empty ledger serves an empty list, not null; a row's title is served and a row with none serves an empty title; a planned run with no reservation is absent. Updated (2026-10-31): ~~a claim records the title~~ is dropped with the claim write.

title: [BE] The comparison endpoint serves the time each run settled
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Every row of `runs` has `settled_at`, RFC 3339, equal to the record's `SettledAt`; none lacks one, because the comparison lists settled runs only.
2. Row order and count, and every other field, are unchanged, so an older page reads the new answer.

title: [BE] A plan whose decision breaks a bound gets one correction round instead of stopping the run
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A decision that breaks any bound listed in `decision.go` triggers exactly one correction round, whose prompt names the broken rule as the validator words it, for example "context line 1 is over 200 bytes".
2. The corrected plan goes through the same re-check, and a plan that is valid on the first round does no second round.
3. A plan still invalid after the correction round stops once as `plan-invalid` with the second round's error.
4. The correction round's model spend counts as plan spend and against the plan stage's budget.
5. Tests: a decision invalid then valid, invalid then invalid, and valid on the first round.

title: [BE] A run records the agent's head sha, and its required checks' result once they settle
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. For a run that opened a pull request, each dispatcher poll finds the agent's last commit: the last commit of the pull request whose GitHub author login is the runner's, taking the repository and number from the row's `pr_url` (a run's `pr_number` is written only at merge).
2. Each poll reads, for every run that opened a pull request and has no `checks_result`, the required checks of that commit: the contexts of the repository's merge rule, read from GitHub.
3. When every required check is terminal it writes `pr_head_sha` and `checks_result` = `green` (all succeeded) or `failing` (any did not) together, once; a row that has `checks_result` is never read again. A pending check, or a required check that has not reported, writes nothing; a run still pending after 24 hours logs `checksPendingStale` and is not counted. A pull request with no commit by the runner's login, or a `pr_url` that does not parse, is written `checks_result` = `unresolved` once, with no `pr_head_sha`, and is never read again.
4. A failed check read logs `checksReadFailed` and leaves the row for the next poll; it never writes `failing` or `unresolved`.
5. The 50 existing pull request runs are settled by the same poll, at most 20 per poll, oldest first; a row with no agent commit is marked `unresolved` and logs `checksNoAgentCommit` once, at that moment. A run behind twenty unresolvable ones is still reached.
6. Tests: pending writes nothing, green, failing, a read error leaves the row, a second poll is a no-op, the 20-per-poll cap, the last agent commit is chosen over an owner's later ones, an unresolved row is marked once and not listed again.
7. A requeue clears both fields with the other settled-run fields, so a retried run does not keep the previous attempt's result.

title: [FE] Statistics shows the run success card above Last 20 runs
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The card is first in the main column, above Last 20 runs, in the page's card frame; the Projects card starts at its top; on the phone it is the first card.
2. Caption "run success"; definition "Run success is the share of runs that end in a PR with passing checks. Higher is better."
3. With 20 or more runs: a shape beside "On target" (90% or more) or "Below target"; the figure at 34px, right-aligned on that baseline, with "target 90%" under it; the lines "Over the trailing 4 weeks (P of R runs)", "Previous 4 weeks: X% (P of R runs)" and "Top stop: CLASS, N of F failures" (omitted with no failures). Updated (2026-11-02): the word is decided on the raw rate and the figure is the whole percent rounded down, so "On target" shows exactly when the rate is at least 90 and the word never disagrees with the number; CLASS reads as the endpoint's id with hyphens turned to spaces ("agent timeout"); one failure reads "1 of 1 failure"; when the previous four weeks have under 20 runs the line reads "Previous 4 weeks: too few runs (P of R runs)", and "Previous 4 weeks: no runs" with none.
4. Under 20 runs: "Too few runs", no figure, and "Only R runs in the trailing 4 weeks; 20 needed for a rate".
5. Loading reads "Reading the run success…" and holds the ready card's height; failed reads "The run success could not be read." with the head alone.
6. With a project chosen the card stays pooled and adds "run success: all projects".
7. Contrast 4.5:1, targets 44x44, no sideways scroll at 320. The 90% is one named constant.

title: [BE] /api/run-success answers the run success rate over the trailing four weeks
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `GET /api/run-success` returns `passed` and `runs` for the 28 days to now and for the 28 days before, and the most common failure class with its count (omitted when there are no failures).
2. A run passed when `outcome` is `pr-opened` and `checks_result` is `green`. The denominator is runs started in the window that finished, excluding owner-cancelled runs; `no-changes` counts as a failure; a run whose pull request result is still pending is left out until it settles; a run whose `checks_result` is `unresolved` is left out of both the passed count and the denominator. Updated (2026-11-02): a run the sweep marked abandoned, which wrote no outcome, counts as a failure of class `abandoned` in the denominator and the failure mix, and one that is both abandoned and cancelled by the owner counts in neither.
3. Under 20 runs in a window the rate is null and the count is returned.
4. One rows-only query projecting `checks_result`, `outcome`, `started_at`, `stop_reason`, `cancelled_by_owner_at` and `state`, capped at 200 rows, with a `runSuccessCapped` log line when the read returns 200 rows; no GitHub call. Updated (2026-11-02): the last two fields are what tell an owner-cancelled run from a failed one and an abandoned run from one still in flight.
5. Tests for each rule above.

title: [BE] A formatting-only check failure is fixed by the formatter, not by a model round
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A run whose only failure is `gofmt` or `web-fmt-check` ends with the formatter's output in the worktree, committed by the build's single commit, and the checks green, with no model round spent.
2. A run with a formatter failure and another failing gate runs the formatter first, then gives the model only the remaining failures.
3. The formatter's edits are committed by the runner's one commit under its own bot login, so the rewrite rate counts them as agent lines.
4. A formatter that changes a file outside the run's diff stops the run and names the file; nothing is committed.
5. The review stage's fix round is formatted the same way before its checks.

title: [BE] A plan-stage failure logs its cause in the plan job
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `plan-stage` logs a failure once, at error level, with the fixed token `planStageFailed`, the ticket and the error as separate attributes, before it wraps the error in `errRunFailed`.
2. The exit code and the `errRunFailed` wrapper are unchanged, and no other command's output changes: `main`'s `runnerFailed` rule is not touched.
3. The logged error is the one `runner.PlanStage` returned, unmodified, for every failure shape it has: the agent failing, a projection miss, and a plan that does not validate.
4. A successful plan stage logs no `planStageFailed` line.
5. Tests: a failing `PlanStage` produces exactly one `planStageFailed` line carrying the error's text; a successful one produces none.

title: [BE] A queued run takes its ticket's current text, size and blockers on each poll
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. On a poll that sees a delegated issue whose run record is in state `queued` with no plan, the record's ticket title, body, size, front-end flag, `blocked_by` and `blocks` are set to the issue's current values in one transaction. A record already equal is not written.
2. A record in any other state (planned, in flight, ended) is not changed, whatever the issue says; the poll still counts it as seen.
3. When the issue's current values would be refused as a new ticket (no size label, `XL`, or a repository off the allowlist), the old record is kept as it was and the refusal is logged; the run is not deleted.
4. Each change logs once with the fixed token `queuedTicketRefreshed`, the run id and the names of the fields changed as separate arguments, never in the message, as `queuedPriorityChanged` does.
5. Tests: a body edited after enqueue reaches the record; a changed blocker list reaches it; a planned record is left as it was; an unchanged record is not written; and values that fail validation leave the record as it was.
6. The existing priority refresh is unchanged.

title: [FE] The project filter lists three projects and opens the rest in place
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. More than three projects, All chosen: the card lists All projects and the first three projects in the card's existing order, then the link "Show all N projects" (N the number added) on its own 52px row (the list's row height, over the 44px floor) at the names' x, in the accent colour and underlined. Never more than three project rows show.
2. Activating the link lists every project in the card, with no inner scroll and no navigation, and the link now reads "Show fewer"; activating that folds back to three. The link is a button with `aria-expanded`, focus stays on it, and Enter and Space both toggle it.
3. Three projects or fewer: no link, and the card reads as it does today.
4. With a project chosen, only that project is listed under the unchosen All projects row, with no link, as today; choosing All restores the folded list.
5. The Overview's "See all N projects", which navigates to the Projects page, is unchanged; this link expands in place.
6. Contrast, targets, reflow and zoom as the rest of the page: the link text at least 4.5:1, a row over the 44px floor, a visible focus ring, no sideways scroll at 320.

title: [FE] Auto-merge moves to Autonomy as a card, and Statistics' second card becomes the rewrite rate
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Autonomy, every width: the status block is a card in the page's card frame (radius 16, padding 26) holding, top to bottom, the AUTO-MERGE caption; the status as a shape beside its words (`Status` in `web/src/stats/auto-merge.tsx` moves with it); the rate and reason lines as the page words them today; and the two who-merges-what bullets (`Rules` moves with it, worded as drawn: "while the rewrite rate over the trailing N PRs is X% or less", window and bar from the endpoint). 2. The "..." sits on the status row at the card's right end: 36x22 visible (the owner's size, was 44x28), 44x44 hit area, accessible name "Auto-merge settings", navigating to Configuration, shown in every status (on, off, held).
3. Desktop: the card is in the left column and the project column starts on the same line as the card's top (within 1px), below the subline, with no caption; the rewrite-rate section starts below the lower of the two.
4. Phone: the status card is a full-width card under the subline, and the project card stays last on the page, under its PROJECTS caption.
5. Statistics, second card: the caption "rewrite rate"; a definition line reading "Rewrite rate is owner lines as a share of agent lines in merged PRs. Lower is better."; the rate line "Rewrite rate over the trailing 10 PRs is X%; limit 10%" (the limit printed whole, not "10.0%"); the key line reading "Median PR is the middle PR's own rewrite rate. Pooled is the same rate over all of a model's lines."; then the plan, build and review models as today. It has no status, no "..." pill and no bullets, and its accessible heading is "rewrite rate".
6. With a project chosen on Statistics, the card's note reads "rate and models: all projects" (it read "gate and models: all projects").
7. The loading and error states of both pages read as the drawings (Autonomy panels 28, 29, 35 and 36 for the status read, plain page text with no card; Statistics' card states are desktop panels 41-42 of `inbox-desktop-v1.svg` and phone panels 58-59 of `inbox-mobile-v1.svg`).

title: [FE] The Autonomy By model block gives each stage its own card and headlines its main model
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Three cards in run order, titled Plan, Build and Review (no "model"), each with a numeral 1, 2, 3 in a ring and "N of M PRs" beside the title. N is the PRs that went through the stage, M the measured PRs. Each card has its own 0-80% axis row. The gap between cards is 24px on desktop and 16px on a phone. One slim card below holds the legend and the measured-figures note.
2. The main model (most PRs in the stage) is row one with full detail: name at the 17px step, PR count, the pooled bar with its three-way split, the pooled rate, and median and p90. A main model under ten PRs says "under ten PRs, so no median" where the median would be.
3. A stage shows at most three rows. "no plan stage", "no review" and "unknown (mixed or no model)" are always shown and count as rows. When more than three would show, the smallest models fold into one "N other models" row with their combined PR count, pooled rate and a thin muted bar. A stage that fits shows every row as itself.
4. The PR strip's lane label reads "plan" (`web/src/autonomy/pr-strip.tsx:23`).
5. On a phone the cards stack at 440 and 320 with no sideways scroll. At the build's 320 content width a long name wraps its count under the name, and the axis labels reduce to 0, 40 and 80.
6. With a project chosen the cards cover that project's figures and count against its PRs (panel 13 reads 13 of 32, 32 of 32 and 30 of 32).
7. Contrast, targets, reflow and zoom hold as on the rest of the page.
8. No back-end or API change: the cards read the served `by_model` rows.

title: [FE] The Projects row shows START greyed out, with a reason, when its phase has nothing to start
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. When a project is reachable, not paused, its snapshot is readable, nothing is in flight, queued or held, no start is pending and the snapshot's `eligible` list is empty, its row shows a START pill, disabled, in the style of the existing disabled START. title: [FE] Statistics names its figures, shows what its colours mean, and pages its cache table
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Each model figure's caption reads "median PR rewrite rate", with "above 10%" on its own line when it is over the bar. A definition line under the card title reads "Rewrite rate is owner lines as a share of agent lines in merged PRs. Lower is better." A key line above the phases reads "Median PR is the middle PR's own rewrite rate. Pooled is the same rate over all of a model's lines."
2. The rate line reads "Rewrite rate over the trailing 10 PRs is X%; limit 10%". The status and the "Merges itself" rule moved to Autonomy. Updated (2026-11-01): the page prints "guide 10%", not "limit 10%", since FRG-256 made the rate a guide.
3. The run strip has a visible legend, one entry per colour listing every kind that shares it: merged; PR open; failed, credential missing, unconfirmed decision; allowance spent, draft PR; cancelled, no changes, other. Bars and legend come from one table so they cannot drift; it holds at 320. The bars' tooltips are not drawn here.
4. The cache table's runs with no per-phase split collapse into one line ("N older runs recorded no cache split; recording began with FRG-121 on 14 October.", N counted from the data) with a "Hide older runs" control; opened, their whole-run share shows as a paged table of their own.
5. "none" reads "no plan stage". Headers read "First request" and "Whole phase", with a definition line under the title ("First request is the phase's opening call; whole phase is every call in it; whole run is every call in the run."). Updated (2026-10-30): on desktop the sub-headers wrap onto two lines, "First" over "request" and "Whole" over "phase", to make room for the Finished column.
6. Each phase's two figures come from the endpoint's numbers (FRG-227), not from parsing its string. Added (2026-10-27): where the page prints a percent from a number, it rounds half to even, as the server's strings do (Go prints 0.625 as 62%, while JavaScript's usual rounding gives 63%), so a printed figure never differs from the server's own string by a point.
7. The cache table is paged with the shared pager (FRG-228): ten a page from 768, five below; range line ("Runs 11-14 of 14"), PREVIOUS and NEXT as in the drawing; it returns to page 1 when the project filter changes; none when everything fits.
8. Contrast, targets, reflow and zoom as the rest of the page.
9. Added (2026-10-30): a column headed "Finished (AEST/AEDT)" (Updated (2026-10-31): the header was ~~Finished~~; on desktop it sits on two lines, "Finished" over "(AEST/AEDT)", like the cache groups' sub-headers), after Provider and before the two cache groups on desktop, and a "Finished (AEST/AEDT)" line under the run line on the phone, the label left and the time right. Cells read like "30 Oct, 11:42": day without a leading zero, three-letter month, comma, 24-hour time, on the fixed Australia/Sydney clock (Updated (2026-10-31): the zone was ~~the viewer's local time~~; reuse `sydneyDateTime` in `web/src/sydney-date-time.ts`, which the Autonomy table already uses, so one instant reads the same on every machine and the same as there), from the endpoint's `settled_at` (FRG-245). The older-runs table carries it between Provider and Whole run. A missing or unreadable value reads "not recorded". It holds at 320.

title: [FE] Autonomy's Data section is always open, with one paged per-PR table
body:
## Acceptance criteria

 1. No disclosure and no chevron: the "Data" heading, "The exact numbers behind these charts." and the rate legend are always visible. The charts' text alternative stays true: the section lists every figure the charts draw.
 2. Order, top to bottom: the tiles table (trend arrow in words), by size, by model by role, by repository, the no-agent-lines note; then the pager; then the per-PR table; nothing below it.
 3. ONE per-PR table, newest first, the PR number a link to the pull request: PR, title, date and time in Sydney (Updated (2026-10-31): ~~date (UTC)~~), run, size, agent lines, owner lines, rate, trailing 10, plan, build, review. The trend table and the models table are gone, and no datum they carried is lost (the oldest nine PRs, which have no trailing-10 value, show "-" under a note that says why).
 4. Two layouts: from 768 each row is two lines (PR, date, run, size, lines, rate and trailing 10 on the first; title and the plan, build and review models on the second); below 768 rows are stacked label-and-value pairs.
 5. Paged, one named constant per breakpoint: ten a page from 768, five below. The pager shows its range ("PRs 1-10 of 34"), PREVIOUS and NEXT as 44px buttons with their words (a disabled one keeps its word), no pager when everything fits, and returns to page 1 when the project filter changes. It sits directly under the overall tables, above the rows. On a phone a second pager sits 16px under the last row.
 6. Choosing a project scopes the overall tables and the per-PR table; the range line counts that project's PRs.
 7. On the phone the project filter card sits above the Data section (panel 20 gives the page order and each block's start).
 8. Contrast, targets, reflow and zoom as the rest of the page: text at least 4.5:1, targets 44x44, no sideways scroll at 320.
 9. A page change moves nothing above the pager; the pager's own position does not change with the rows.
10. Added (2026-10-30): the surface serves every measured merge in `prs`, so the one table can list them all: `renderPRs` (`cmd/surface/rewrite.go:173`) no longer stops at the newest `dispatcher.TrailingPRs` (10) and serves every merge the read holds, up to `measuredShown` (200, `cmd/surface/autonomy.go:110`). The trailing-10 rate and its tiles are still computed over the newest ten. Two Go tests: more than ten measured merges are all served, newest first; a project's scoped answer holds only its own.
11. Added (2026-10-31): the per-PR strip keeps drawing the newest ten PRs, as drawn, now that `prs` is longer: its dot count and its label name ten, and the paged table is the only place all of them appear.
12. Added (2026-10-31), as drawn: the per-PR table's date column shows each PR's `merged_at` in the `Australia/Sydney` zone with date and time, 24-hour and no year, as `17 Oct, 07:20`; its header reads `Date Finished (AEST/AEDT)` (Updated (2026-10-31): the header was ~~Date, Sydney~~; on the phone it is a full-width line of its own above the six figure pairs), and the first note begins `Trailing 10 is the rewrite rate` with no zone sentence before it (Updated (2026-10-31): the note was opened by ~~Times are Sydney time.~~). The zone is fixed, so the same instant reads the same on every machine, and the header names AEST/AEDT because Sydney is on AEDT from October to April. Nothing else on the page changes zone.

title: [BE] The comparison endpoint serves each phase's cache share as two numbers

1. Each run carries `build_first_share`, `build_phase_share`, `plan_first_share` and `plan_phase_share`, each a number from 0 to 1 or null.

title: [FE] Statistics filters its run history by project
body:
## Acceptance criteria

Same harness and bands as FRG-225: 1280, 1024, 768, 440 and 320.

1. **The card.** On `/stats`, the card matches FRG-225's AC1: the "projects" caption, the "Project filter" radiogroup, All first, every served project with its state chip, rows at least 44px, a 20px ring and a 10px dot, exactly one checked. There is no chevron, tick, START/STOP/RESUME or visible "Showing".
2. **Placement.** At each band, Statistics has two columns exactly when the Overview does. Two columns: run history sits above the rewrite-rate card in the main column, and the filter column stands alone on the right. The top of the "projects" caption equals the top of the page's heading (±1px), and the card's top equals the run history block's top (±1px). The drawing opens the page with a "statistics" caption, as Configuration's does (`web/src/pages/config.tsx:57-59`); if the built page lacks it, this ticket adds it. One column: run history, then the rewrite-rate card, then the filter column last, in DOM and Tab order.
3. **A project narrows the run history.** Choosing a project leaves All (unchecked) above that project alone. Then the strip shows only the rows whose `repo` matches, case-insensitively, oldest first. The caption counts them and names the project: "Last 7 runs, alvintoh/forge-wingman", or "Last run, …" for one. The merged count counts only their merged runs. Rows with an empty `repo` show only under All. Each bar keeps its spoken words. Choosing All restores the full history.
4. **Pooled figures say so.** With a project chosen, the rewrite-rate card's rate line and models by phase read the same as under All, and "rate and models: all projects" sits under the rate line. Under All, that line is absent. The card still reads `/api/autonomy` with no `repo`. While the cached-share table is on the page, its intro line names it as covering all projects whenever a project is chosen.
5. **No data.** For a listed project with none of the served rows, the strip keeps its 26px and reads "No run for <owner/name> in the last N runs.", where N is the number of rows served. No merged count shows. With no rows at all, the existing "No run has settled yet." stands.
6. **The URL.** Same as FRG-225's AC6, on `/stats`: replace, reload, case, and the unknown, empty or non-string value falling back to All with a cleaned URL. The strip follows the URL at once, as the Overview's Actions do. The menu's Statistics link carries `?project=` from the Overview and from Autonomy. From Statistics, the menu's Overview and Autonomy links carry it. Statistics keeps `aria-current="page"`.
7. **No layout shift.** Updated (2026-10-30): ~~With /api delayed, CLS on load is no worse than the origin/main build at every band.~~ CLS on load stays under 0.1 at every band. The filter column is last on a phone and a tablet, so it moves once when the rewrite-rate card above it grows as `/api/autonomy` answers; no card above it moves. Measured on the production build at 440 and 768: 0.0355 and 0.0225, against main's 0.0265 and 0.008, where main's cached-share intro line is the element that moves. Choosing a project or All moves nothing in the main column: the run history and rewrite-rate tops stay put (±0.5px). The strip's line keeps 26px in the loading, error, empty and filled states.
8. **The projects list fails.** The filter column shows the Overview's error panel and TRY AGAIN. The run history still follows the URL's project, as the Overview's Actions do.
9. **WCAG 2.2 AA.** The same checks as FRG-225's AC9: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for the ring and dot, every radio a Tab stop with a focus outline of at least 2px, Space and Enter choose, the full `owner/name` as the accessible name, no sideways scroll at 320 with a 40-character name, and zoom not blocked.

title: [FE] Autonomy filters its rewrite figures by project
body:
## Acceptance criteria

Each is checked by headless Playwright against the production build, with `/api` stubbed, at 1280x800, 1024x768, 768x1024, 440x763 (scale 3, touch) and 320x700.

1. **The card.** `/autonomy` shows a "projects" caption and a radiogroup named "Project filter". "All projects" comes first, then every project `/api/projects` serves, in its order, each with the Overview's state chip (running, stopping, stopped, checking; none otherwise). Exactly one radio is checked: All by default. Each row is one radio, at least 44px tall and the card's full width. The bullet is a 20px ring with a 2px border; the checked one has a 10px accent dot. There is no chevron, no tick, no START/STOP/RESUME and no visible "Showing".
2. **Placement.** At each band, Autonomy has two columns exactly when the Overview does at that viewport. Two columns: the status block is on the left and the filter column on the right, with the card 368px wide. The top of the "projects" caption equals the top of the status block (±1px). The rewrite section starts below both, full width. One column: the filter column is last on the page, after the Data disclosure (or after the state card), in DOM and Tab order.
3. **A project scopes the section.** Choosing a project (click, Space or Enter) leaves "All projects" (unchecked) above that project alone (checked). The section then shows what `/api/autonomy?repo=<owner/name>` serves: the heading reads "Rewrite rate, <owner/name>"; under it, "<owner/name> only: N of the M measured PRs." (N is that project's PR count in the unscoped `by_repo`, matched case-insensitively; M is the sum of the unscoped `by_repo` counts, `unattributed` included; the line is absent when M is 0); the tiles, trend, strip, by size, by model and Data tables are the scoped answer's; by repository has one row; the trend's caption names the project, never "all repositories" or "gate, pools every repository". Choosing All restores the pooled section and the full list.
4. **The gate stays pooled and says so.** With a project chosen, the status, rate line and reason read the same as under All, and "gate: all projects" sits under them. Under All, that line is absent.
5. **No data.** A listed project with no measured PR shows the state card "no measured PRs" with "Rates for <owner/name> appear once one of its runner PRs has merged." and the scope line "<owner/name> only: 0 of the M measured PRs." A project whose PRs carry no agent lines shows "no agent lines" with "<owner/name>'s merged PRs carry no agent lines, so there is nothing to divide." The All-projects copy is unchanged.
6. **The URL.** Choosing sets `?project=<owner/name>` by replace, so `history.length` is unchanged. A reload keeps the choice. A value in different case checks the right row and scopes. An unknown, empty or non-string value (`?project=`, `?project=true`) settles on All, and the URL is cleaned to `/autonomy` by replace. No `/api/autonomy` request carries that value: `?repo=` is sent only for a project the list holds. With a project chosen, the menu's Overview and Autonomy links carry `?project=`, and Autonomy keeps `aria-current="page"`. The Configuration link and the header icon do not carry it.
7. **No layout shift.** With `/api` delayed, CLS on load is no worse than the origin/main build at every band. Choosing a project or All moves nothing above the rewrite section: the status block's top and the All row's top stay put (±0.5px). While the scoped answer loads, the section keeps the figures on screen, is `aria-busy="true"`, and its heading still names the scope of those figures. The heading and the figures change together.
8. **The projects list fails.** The filter column shows "The projects could not be read." with TRY AGAIN (the Overview's panel), and TRY AGAIN re-reads the list. The section shows the pooled figures under "Rewrite rate". While the list loads, the column shows "Reading the projects…". Added (2026-10-27): when the list is empty the column shows only "No project is listed.", with no radiogroup and no All projects row, as panels 26 and 33 draw it; the choice then stays All and no scoped read is made.
9. **WCAG 2.2 AA.** All text is at least 4.5:1 against its real background, including the scope and gate lines and the chips' white on fill. The ring and the dot are at least 3:1 against the card. Every radio is a Tab stop with a visible focus outline of at least 2px. Space and Enter choose. ~~Each radio's accessible name is the full ~~`~~~~owner/name~~~~`. Updated (2026-10-27): each radio's accessible name is the name it displays. At 320, with All and with a 40-character `owner/name` chosen, there is no sideways page scroll and each row stays at least 44px tall. The viewport meta does not block zoom.

title: [SLICE] The owner sets N in Config settings, with the recommended N shown beside it
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Config settings has "Runs at once (N)", a whole number from 1 to the platform cap; a value outside it is refused with 400; the default is today's live value (2), so a deploy changes nothing.
2. Admission uses the owner's N at the next poll; lowering it never stops a run in flight.
3. The tuner stops writing N. It keeps recording its observations and computes a recommended N by the same rule (up one after 5 stable observations, halve past 1.5x the solo median); Config shows "Recommended: R" beside N with the reason in words.
4. The recommendation changes nothing by itself.
5. Drawn first (`/proto-draw`); WCAG 2.2 AA, mobile-first.
6. A "USE R" button beside the recommendation, shown only while R differs from the number in the field, fills the field with R and does not save.
7. Preset buttons "5", "10" and "15" beside the field fill it and do not save; the preset equal to the field's number is shown selected (pressed, with a tick); a preset above the platform cap is not shown.

Added (2026-11-03): criteria 6 and 7, owner's review of the drawing. Both only fill the field, so criterion 4 still holds and SAVE still saves.

title: [SLICE] Statistics shows runs in flight against each concurrency limit, and which limit held each run
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. When a poll holds a run, the dispatcher records the reason (`concurrency`, `repo-busy`, `review-wip`, `large-cap`, `blocked`, budget, and `job-limit`, `breaker`, `paused`, `peak-hours`, `provider-down`, `no-estimate`) at most once per run, reason and Sydney day, so the held counts do not grow with every poll (`internal/dispatcher/admit.go:225-238` names the conditions).
2. A Concurrency card shows the trailing-30-day peak runs in flight beside the live N, the per-repo cap, review WIP and the platform cap.
3. The card lists held-run counts by reason for the trailing 30 days, largest first, omitting zeros; with none it reads "No run was held."
4. The figures are computed from stored rows at read time; the only new cost is one write per new hold.
5. Drawn first (`/proto-draw`); WCAG 2.2 AA, mobile-first, no layout shift.

Updated (2026-11-03): criterion 1 counts every hold condition, not six: the platform cap, circuit breaker, owner pause, peak hours, a halted provider and a failed estimate are holds too, named `job-limit`, `breaker`, `paused`, `peak-hours`, `provider-down` and `no-estimate` in the same short style; and days are Sydney calendar days, the owner's, not UTC (owner).

title: [SLICE] Statistics drops the Allowance card, and the surface drops the endpoint behind it
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The Statistics page draws no Allowance card and no "allowance" label; the run history and the auto-merge card keep their places and the page reflows without a gap, on the desktop and the phone, as the redrawn panels show.
2. Nothing in `web/src` reads `/api/providers` (a grep returns none); `GET /api/providers`, its handler (`cmd/surface/providers.go`), its tests and any store reader that only it used are deleted; a reader the dispatcher also uses stays. Before deleting each symbol, grep its callers and report the counts.
3. `GET /api/providers` answers 404 through the `/api/` not-found handler, as any unknown route does.
4. No dispatcher behaviour changes: the plan windows and the budget guard are untouched and their tests stay green.
5. WCAG 2.2 AA, mobile-first CSS, and no layout shift from the removal.

title: [BE] The Autonomy figures can be scoped to one repository
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. With `repo` absent the answer is byte-identical to today's.
2. With `repo=<r>` the tiles, trend series, by-size, by-model, by-repository and PR rows are computed over the samples whose `Repo` equals `<r>` (`internal/dispatcher/rewrite.go:142-149`); an unknown repository answers the empty shape, never an error. **Updated (2026-10-24):** "equals" compares without case, as GitHub names a repository and as `cmd/surface/merge.go:105` does.
3. The `auto_merge` block (status, rate, window, limit, reason) is computed over ALL samples whatever `repo` says, because the gate pools every repository (`renderAutoMerge`, `cmd/surface/autonomy.go:130`); a test pins that the gate does not move when the answer is scoped.
4. The value is validated like the other repository inputs (the length bound `maxRepository` in `cmd/surface/projects.go`); a malformed value is a 400. **Updated (2026-10-24):** `repo=` present but empty, a repeated `repo`, an unparseable query, an over-bound value and a value that is not `owner/name` are all a 400, and the store is not read; only an absent `repo` serves the pooled answer, and unrelated parameters are ignored.

title: [SLICE] Cancel run follow-ups from the independent review of the cancel PR
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. **Retry of a cancelled run.** Decide, and record in `docs/adr/0021-a-cancel-records-the-run-and-leaves-the-pr.md`, whether a stale second tab may retry a run that was just cancelled. Today it can: a cancel does not bump `attempt`, so the stale retry passes the guard and the requeue clears the cancel (`cmd/surface/retry.go`). The ADR calls retry "the un-cancel"; if that stays, say that a stale tab is covered by it; if not, the handler refuses with a reason word, with a test. **Decided (2026-10-26):** it is refused, with reason `cancelled` (the word merge uses); a cancelled record is never sent to GitHub, and the store answers `merged` (a merge by the owner or by the dispatcher's poll) before `cancelled` in its transaction; the ADR names an operator's requeue as the only un-cancel.
2. **Cancel state survives leaving the page.** Cancel state moves from `web/src/inbox/section.tsx` into the provider where merge and retry state live (a `useCancels` hook), so leaving `/` mid-cancel keeps the failure words, the announcement and the in-flight dedup.
3. **Added (2026-10-24):** the owner can cancel a stopped run from its row sheet, so a stopped run that will not be retried leaves the inbox. Today the sheet offers Retry on a stopped row and Cancel only on a run waiting on the owner (`web/src/inbox/row-sheet.tsx`), so 12 old stopped runs (6 to 18 days old, mostly for tickets already Done) cannot be cleared. A stopped run that is cancelled is recorded as cancelled, leaves the inbox, and a retry from a stale tab still follows criterion 1; the dialog says the run is left as it is; the store and handler tests cover a stopped run.
4. **Added (2026-10-26):** a stopped run the owner cancelled raises no stuck-run notice and no exhausted-retries notice: `internal/store/stuck.go` and the transient-stop listing (`TransientStops`) skip a cancelled row, because it is no longer the owner's to retry.
5. **Added (2026-10-26, drawing approved by the owner):** the cancel confirm names the repository and the ticket for both a waiting and a stopped run, as the drawn panels show.

~~3. A hung request ends.~~ ~~4. One dialog lifecycle.~~ ~~5. One JSON check and one status word.~~ Moved to v2 (2026-10-24).

1. Each poll records the names of the team's Linear projects; a project added or renamed in Linear shows in the record after the next poll.
2. A poll that cannot read the projects keeps the last record and does not empty it; the rest of the poll is unaffected.
3. The record holds project names only, nothing else Linear returns.
4. The surface can read the record and cannot write it; the runner's access is unchanged.
5. Nothing else in the poll changes: dispatch order, limits, and the reach and snapshot records.

title: [BE] One listed repository the token cannot read marks every dispatcher poll Failed
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. With one listed repository unreadable and another readable, the poll succeeds and says which repository failed.
2. The readable repository's merges are still measured.
3. When every listed repository is unreadable, the poll still fails.
4. The reachability record for the unreadable repository still reads cannot-read.

title: [INFRA] The webhook's identity is refused the owner database
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A write to a document in `owner` using the webhook's identity is refused. It is checked by an actual write, not by reading the policy.
2. The webhook still records a delivered ticket event in the default database as before.
3. The plan changes the webhook's datastore binding and no other identity's.

title: [BE] The owner adds and removes a project from the command line
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `runner project-add` stores a project, a Linear project name and its repository, in the `owner` database, and says what it stored.
2. Adding a repository that is already listed is refused and names it; nothing changes.
3. A repository not written as owner/name is refused before anything is written.
4. `runner project-remove` removes a listed project; removing one that is not listed says so and changes nothing.
5. Run under an account that is not the owner's, either command refuses and writes nothing.

title: [BE] The dispatcher records whether it can reach each listed repository
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. After each poll every listed repository has a record saying reachable or cannot-read, with the reason and when it was checked.
2. A repository added since the last poll reads checking until the first poll that covers it.
3. One the token cannot read reads cannot-read with the reason; one it can read reads reachable.
4. The record follows access: revoking the token's access shows cannot-read on the next poll, and restoring it shows reachable on the next.
5. Admission is unchanged: the record is a report, and no admission or dispatch decision reads it.
6. A failed write of the record neither stops the poll nor refuses a ticket.

title: [BE] A project's phase can be stopped, then resumed, without cancelling a run
body:

2. Runs in flight when it stops run to their end and settle as they would have. A stop never cancels one.
3. A ticket whose plan stage has settled still claims its build.
4. Tickets delegated but not started stay delegated and are held, and the project's state reports how many.
5. The project reads stopping while any run of it is in flight and stopped when none is. Resume makes the held tickets claimable again as the limits allow, with no re-delegation.
6. Another project is unaffected by a stop.

title: [BE] The dispatcher is woken when a run finishes, so a freed slot refills in seconds
body:

2. A wake that fails does not fail the run or change its recorded outcome; the scheduled poll still picks the next ticket up.
3. A run that records no outcome wakes nothing.
4. With no run finishing, the number of polls a day does not rise.

title: [BE] An unplanned M or L ticket is admitted to its plan stage while another run builds in the same repository
body:
## Acceptance criteria

2. An S ticket, which has no plan stage and no recorded files, is still held while a build is in flight in the same repository.

Updated (2026-10-19): A build-stage claim with no recorded write set, or one beside an in-flight run that has none, is still held; two runs whose write sets are both recorded share the repository, as before (an overlap is handled when the PR opens). title: [INFRA] The surface is deployed, so it can read its own secret
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A service account exists for the surface, distinct from every run job's identity (runner, model, publisher, pr_review, dispatcher, webhook).
2. The service is deployed from the same image recipe (`CMD=surface`), built for linux/amd64, and reads back as running in the project.

title: [BE] The run has a 90-minute cap, and the build loop, the review pass and the final steps each get their own budget
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The run cap is 90 minutes in `internal/runner/loop.go` and in `.github/workflows/model.yml`, each stating where the other lives; a test fails when the two disagree.
2. The build loop (build rounds, check rounds and guard probes) is bounded at 60 minutes from the run's start.
3. The review pass and its fix round are bounded at 25 minutes from the review's own start, whatever the build used.
4. A review cut at its budget records that reason, and the PR opens as a draft naming the unresolved findings (FR-28).
5. 5 minutes of the cap are kept for the commit, bundle and report steps.
6. No stage starts a round its own budget cannot finish.
7. The PRD's NFR-1 states the 90-minute cap and the three budgets.
8. Tests cover each budget's boundary; every new guard is mutation-tested.

title: [BE] Transient requeue runs whenever it is otherwise eligible, with no level check
body:

2. A transient stop is requeued with no level set, within the existing requeue limit.

title: [BE] The dispatcher moves a delegated ticket to In Progress when it claims the run
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Claiming a run sets the ticket In Progress; the state id is resolved per team from the team's states and never hardcoded.
2. The ticket's manual order is read before the change and restored after it, then read back, because a state change rewrites it.
3. A ticket already In Review, Done or Canceled is not touched.
4. A requeue or an abandon returns the ticket to the state it had before the claim.
5. A failed Linear write is logged once with the reason as a separate field and never fails the run.
6. The repo's `CLAUDE.md` work-in-progress count excludes tickets delegated to the runner, because the dispatcher's own review WIP limit already bounds that lane.

title: [BE] The rewrite endpoint serves the by-model, per-group and chart figures the dashboard draws
body:

1. `by_model.{plan,build,review}`: pooled rate, count and the review-found/owner-change/unlabelled split per model.
2. Every group also carries median, p90 (from ten PRs), `no_agent_lines_prs` and `no_agent_owner_lines`.
3. `by_repo` carries a per-repository average.
4. A `rate_value` number sits beside every rate text; no agent lines is a null.
5. `bars` comes from the Go constants (the 10% auto-merge bar), so the web copies no number.
6. Each tile carries `previous_rate_value` and `trend`, flat within 0.5 points.
7. The figures are read from the projected measured rows.

title: [BE] The surface shows and sets the auto-merge switch
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `GET /api/autonomy` carries `auto_merge` with `switch_on` (the owner's setting, on when no document exists), `rate_allows` (the trailing-10 rate over ten measured PRs is 10% or less and no auto-merged PR was reverted, from the same rule the dispatcher uses), `rate_value`, `limit` (the 10% bar read from the Go constant) and `effective` (both true), all computed in Go.
2. `POST /api/auto-merge` with `{enabled}` sets the switch through the same store type the `runner auto-merge` command uses, and answers the new state.
3. The request names only the setting; it writes only the `dispatch/auto-merge` document and nothing else.
4. A switch that cannot be read is reported as off with the reason, never as on.
5. *Updated (2026-10-19):* the surface's service account holds `roles/datastore.user` on the project's Firestore database, and the limit to the `dispatch/auto-merge` document is enforced by the endpoint (AC3) and its test. Google's Firestore IAM documents conditions by time and by database only, never by document path, so a one-document grant is not available. Residual risk: a compromised surface could write any Firestore document; it is reachable only behind IAP, and the same holds for the surface's existing writes (peak mode). Revisit if the surface gains a write endpoint that moves money.

title: [BE] The surface merges a PR as the owner
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The server derives the repository and PR number from the run row and never from the client; the request body carries only `expected_head_sha`.
2. The merge is refused unless the PR is open, not a draft, its checks are green and no provisional decision is unconfirmed, each refusal with its own reason.
3. It calls GitHub's merge with `merge_method` squash and `sha` set to `expected_head_sha`; a 409 or 405 from GitHub returns its reason to the page.
4. A PR that is already merged answers success.
5. A successful merge records `merged_by_owner_at` and the merged sha on the run row.
6. Each inbox row carries `wait_reason`, one of `front-end`, `size-l`, `sampled`, `auto-merge-off`, `unconfirmed-decision`, `draft`, `checks-not-green`, computed in Go; the first four never block the merge.
7. The GitHub credential is read from the surface's own secret and is never present in a run job's environment.

Updated (2026-10-17): the auto-merge status the inbox statistics show (`auto_merge`, the switch and the rate's verdict) moved to its own ticket, which also sets the switch.

title: [BE] The autonomy endpoint returns the rewrite rate as a trend, per-PR figures, sizes, models and repositories
