title: [BE] The transient classifier reads the failed job's log tail
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The record step fetches the failed job's log through the Actions API with a read-only token and keeps only a bounded tail.
2. `ClassifyTransient` runs on that tail: a stored log holding a proxy read error classes `module-proxy`, one holding none classes nothing.
3. The log text is never written to the run row, only the class.
4. A missing token or an unreadable log records the run without a class and fails nothing.
5. Tests cover each class, no match, a missing token and an unreadable log.

title: [BE] Runs with overlapping write sets share a repository; a true conflict resolves by rebase and requeue
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Two build-stage runs in one repository with recorded, intersecting write sets are both admitted.
2. A run with no recorded write set (an S run, or one never planned) still holds the repository against every other run, as today.
3. A PR whose rebase conflicts is requeued once and then stopped with `rebase-conflict`, unchanged.
4. An M or L PR whose changed files touch another in-flight run's write set opens normally; the comment on `planOverlap` (`cmd/runner/pr_meta.go`) is corrected to match.
5. Each admission that overlaps an in-flight write set logs `admittedOverlapping` with both run ids, so the conflict rate can be compared with the `rebase-conflict` count.
6. Tests cover intersecting known sets admitted, an unknown set held, and the plan stage unchanged.

title: [BE] A queued row that already has an outcome is claimed and its merged ticket rebuilt
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A `queued` or `planned` row with an `outcome` is never claimed, is settled to `claimed`, and is logged by run id.
2. The path that left it queued is fixed: an ended row that is still `queued` can be requeued instead of refused as dispatchable.
3. Tests cover a queued row and a planned row with an outcome and a PR url.
4. A genuine requeue (outcome cleared) still claims normally.

title: [BE] A finished run's reservation can stay in the ledger and defer every build
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. *Updated (2026-10-16):* a ledger reservation older than its stage's window whose run row has an outcome, has a stop reason, is no longer claimed, or is missing is dropped by the next sweep, and the row is left as it was.
2. A reservation inside its window is never dropped by this step, even when its row has an outcome.
3. The plan-stage window applies to a plan-stage reservation and the build window to a build one.
4. A claimed row with no outcome is left to the existing abandon path.
5. Each reservation dropped this way is logged once, with the run id and key.
6. Guided runs and the admission of other runs are unchanged.

title: [INFRA] The dispatcher's runtime settings live in OpenTofu, so an apply cannot reset them
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `tofu plan` against the live project shows no change to the dispatcher job.
2. The ~~four~~ three settings are declared in `infra/` with today's values.
3. `infra/README.md` says where a dispatcher setting is changed, so the next one is not set by hand.

Updated (2026-11-03): criterion 2 covers three settings. `WINGMAN_REPOS` no longer exists: the repository list moved to the owner database (adr/0019), nothing reads the key, and the live job does not carry it; the README says where that list is changed. Criterion 1 also needed the job to ignore the client labels gcloud stamps on a hand-run update.

title: A run records the model that built it, so MiMo can be tried against DeepSeek on stated limits
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. ~~A settled run's record names the model each phase actually ran on, including when the ticket carried no model label.~~ **Updated (2026-10-15):** each step already records the model it ran on (`Step.Model`, `internal/runner/summary.go:72`), so the comparison credits a run to the model its build-phase steps ran on, and falls back to the ticket's label only when a record has no build step.
2. The comparison view lists DeepSeek default runs and MiMo runs as separate rows, with tickets, passes, cost per ticket and wall-clock minutes per ticket.
3. A `command-code/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` run is priced from its tokens at $0.435 in / $0.87 out / $0.0036 cache read per 1M and counts against the plan's windows and model cap.
4. A MiMo run is never held for DeepSeek's peak hours.
5. The post-open rework rate is reported per build model over a window.
6. **Added (2026-10-15, from review of PR #159):** a model with no measured run reports its rewrite rate as "not measured", never 0.0%; a run with a commit GitHub gave no line counts for is left out of its model's rate, as the trailing rate already treats it; and a run whose build moved to another model part way (a fallback among them) is credited to no model.

title: The build agent gets the stack guidance the interactive lane reads
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The build projection includes the stack packs for the repo's languages and tooling, and the plan projection does not change. **Updated (2026-10-15):** the packs are chosen by the repo's declared stack, so every ticket in the repo gets the same set.
2. The projection still sends the agent to no path outside its working directory.
3. The projection's measured size is recorded, and the generator fails when it drifts past the recorded size plus a tolerance.
4. Prompt-cache share on the build phase stays within the current 96–98% band after the change.

title: The runner's review catches what green gates miss before the PR opens
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The review pass reports a finding when a changed guard can be removed and the tests still pass. **Updated (2026-10-15):** this is proved by breaking each changed guard in turn and running the tests; a guard whose break leaves every test green is the finding.
2. The review pass reports a finding when code outside the diff (a caller, a test name, a doc) no longer matches the changed behaviour.
3. The review pass reports a finding when code is added after an early return that skips it for the cases the feature exists for.
4. The review pass reports a finding when a convention the build rules state (no ticket ids in comments, tests for each fail-closed path) is broken in the diff.
5. A finding from AC1–AC4 drives a fix round before the PR opens, and the PR body lists each one and how it was resolved.
6. A run with no findings opens its PR exactly as it does today.

title: [BE] The review path and the cap wiring keep their coverage
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* **AC1:** A test drives OmpHarness.Agent for a model with no configured ceiling and asserts no models.yml is written, so harness_omp.go:201 runs either way.
* **AC2:** The hermetic ompModels test stays, covering the formatting and selection cases a config cannot express.
* **AC3:** When a model carries a cap again, an end-to-end positive case comes back with it.
* **AC4:** Added (2026-10-15): pr-review.yml's fallback for an unset WINGMAN_PR_REVIEW_MODELS is a review list the runner accepts, and a test asserts it matches the configured review list. The existing assertion covered run.yml and review-smoke.yml only.
* **AC5:** Added (2026-10-15): The repository variable WINGMAN_PR_REVIEW_MODELS names a list the runner accepts. Set to command-code/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor; it had named laguna, which #154 made the build fallback.

title: [BE] A free model is proven with the smoke before it is configured
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* **AC1:** A candidate free id is proven by a live `plan-smoke.yml` dispatch before it is written into `providers.json` or `models.json`, and the run id is recorded beside it.
* **AC2:** A test or a named review step fails when a free id in the config has no recorded smoke run.
* **AC3:** ADR 0015's free-tier note points at the smoke as the proof, not at the vendor's model list.

title: [BE] A free rung of two or more models must carry a measured date
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `validate` refuses a free rung of two or more models whose `measured_on` is `unmeasured`, naming the provider; a one-model rung may stay `unmeasured`.
2. Tests cover a two-model undated rung (refused), a one-model undated rung (accepted), a two-model dated rung (accepted), and the embedded configuration loading.
3. ADR 0015 states why command-code's rung is `unmeasured`, that gemini's was measured 2026-10-11, and the rule above, so the next swap follows it.

title: [BE] A second usable free model or a single free rung is stated
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* **AC1:** Either a second `:free` id is proven by `plan-smoke.yml` and configured as the free rung's second entry and the review's second vendor, or ADR 0015 states the free tier is one rung and the review one vendor, naming the consequence.
* **AC2:** Whichever holds, a test asserts it, so the state cannot drift silently.
* **AC3:** Review fallback behaviour is unchanged wherever it still applies.

title: [BE] A failed plan-smoke names why the agent failed
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* **AC1:** A failed `plan-smoke` model reports the agent's stderr tail, redacted the way the review smoke redacts it.
* **AC2:** The tail is bounded to a fixed length, so a chatty failure cannot flood the job log.
* **AC3:** A test drives a failing agent and asserts its stderr reaches the reported line.
* **AC4:** A passing model's output is unchanged.

title: [BE] The instructions say where an agent-lane plan belongs
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* **AC1:** `CLAUDE.md` states that a plan for an agent-lane ticket belongs in the ticket's description, never a comment, with the reason the run reads only the description.
* **AC2:** It names how a ticket is delegated — Linear's `delegate` set to the agent id the dispatcher's job acts for.
* **AC3:** The section's lead sentence no longer counts the bullets it introduces.

title: [BE] The agent prompts are re-stamped from the poly-mind master
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* **AC1:** The six `.claude/agents/*.md` files equal the `compose-agents.py <master> <repo>` output for the master at the stamp.
* **AC2:** Each agent's `## This repo` section is byte-identical to the one that was there before the stamp.
* **AC3:** No agent recommends `ling-3.1-flash:free`; the id survives only in the sentence that records its retirement.
* **AC4:** `compose-agents.py <master> <repo> --check` exits 0 afterwards.

title: [BE] A poll reads the run history once, not once per queued ticket
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* **AC1:** A poll reads the settled run history at most once, however many candidates are queued.
* **AC2:** TryClaim still reads the run row and ledger in its transaction, so two polls cannot both claim one run.
* **AC3:** Updated (2026-10-15): A test counts reads for one poll with 12 queued candidates and fails above 300. At about 100 polls a day that keeps reads under 30k, about 40% below the free quota.
* **AC4:** Admission decisions are unchanged: existing dispatcher and store tests pass.
* **AC5:** Added (2026-10-15): While a non-budget limit (open-PR WIP or concurrency) already holds every candidate, a poll defers them without reading the settled run history.
* **AC6:** Added (2026-10-15): The size estimate reads only the latest N settled runs of that size, so no poll read grows with total run history.

title: [FE] Each provider window is its own bullet, and a phone stacks the rows
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The Window usage cell lists each window as its own bullet with the name and the amounts, and shows the word `unknown` when the provider reports none.
2. From 380px wide up, every bullet is one line; below 380px a bullet may wrap; the amounts are never cut off at any width from 320 to 1600.
3. Below the `md` breakpoint (768px) each plan stacks as a block with labelled Price, Window usage and Terms; at `md` and up it is the same table as before.
4. The header row stays available to screen readers when it is visually hidden.
5. No page scrolls sideways at any width from 320 to 1600, and the nav links keep their 44px targets.
6. A `/fe-evidence` table (s, m, l, xl) is attached to the PR.

title: [BE] A run stuck in the queue or stopped with no PR raises one notice naming why and what clears it
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A run row queued or stopped-without-a-PR for longer than DEFAULT_STUCK_RUN_AFTER (proposal 4 hours) raises one notice naming the run, its state, its stop reason or deferral reason, and the command that clears it (`runner requeue -run-id <id>` for a stopped run).
2. A run deferred because its blocker is not yet Done for longer than the limit is named in a notice together with the blocker's identifier and state.
3. A notice is raised once per run per state: not again on later polls, and again only when the run's state or reason changes.
4. A run that moves on (dispatched, merged, requeued) stops being reported.
5. The check takes no action on any run and spends nothing.
6. Tests cover a stopped run beyond and under the limit, a blocked run, no repeat on a second poll, and a run that moves on.

title: [BE] A run that stopped on a classified transient fault is requeued up to a limit, each attempt recorded
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Updated (2026-10-16): the runner classifies a stop from its recorded detail against a closed, tested list of transient signatures (a Go module proxy read error, a network timeout, a lost runner) and records the matched class on the run row. Reading the failing job's own log is moved to the follow-up ticket FRG-154, because nothing the record job receives is a log: the 2026-10-16 replay over every live run classified none, and the motivating runs carry only a link or an empty detail. An abandoned claim carries no class, since it is as likely cancelled by the owner as lost.
2. At autonomy level 1 or above, the dispatcher requeues a stopped run whose recorded class is on the list, recording each automatic attempt with its class.
3. At most DEFAULT_TRANSIENT_REQUEUES (proposal 2) automatic requeues per run; after that the run stays stopped and raises a notice.
4. A stop with no matching class (an agent timeout, a failing check gate, a plan the agent could not produce) is never requeued automatically.
5. An automatic requeue never bypasses admission: the budget ceiling, the review WIP limit and the breaker apply to it exactly as to a new run.
6. At level 0 nothing is requeued automatically.
7. Tests cover each listed class, an unlisted failure, the attempt limit, level 0, and a held admission.

title: [FE] The house fonts load and the nav link meets the touch target
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `design/gen_theme_css.py` in the vault emits `@font-face` rules for IBM Plex Sans 400 and 600 and IBM Plex Mono 400 and 600 with `font-display: swap` and `format("woff2")`; `theme.css` is regenerated there and copied downstream, never edited by hand in the product repo.
2. The four `.woff2` files are copied into `web/public/fonts/` (the vault's downstream copy rules updated if they exclude them) and the sweep shows `document.fonts` listing all four as `loaded`.
3. The nav link's box is at least 44px tall and 44px wide (padding, not a bigger font), and its focus ring is still visible.
4. No page scrolls sideways at 320px, and body contrast stays at or above 4.5:1 on the page background.
5. A `/fe-sweep` table (s, m, l, xl) is attached to the PR after `/pr-review`.

title: [BE] The runner's check gate runs the same web checks CI does
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. When a run's diff touches `web/`, the check gate also runs the web job's steps (install with the frozen lockfile, lint, fmt:check, build) in the checks image and names the failing step.
2. A web failure feeds the same fix loop as a Go check failure, so the build agent sees the output and gets its fix round.
3. A run whose diff does not touch `web/` skips the web steps and behaves as today.
4. The checks image provides bun, or the ticket records why it cannot and what runs the web steps instead.
5. Tests cover a web lint failure, a fmt:check failure, a build failure, a pass, and a diff with no `web/` change.

title: [SLICE] The run statistics view and plan-list print each run's prompt-cache share
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `runner plan-list` prints, for each plan, the trailing runs' cached share per phase (first request and whole phase) beside the existing columns.
2. The surface's run view lists each run's cached share for the build and plan phases, and shows `not recorded` for a run that predates FRG-121, never 0%.
3. A run with no requests in a phase prints that phase as `none`, not as a share.
4. Tests cover a run with a share, a run without one, and an empty list.

title: [SLICE] The surface shows the autonomy level, its evidence and its history
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `GET /api/autonomy` returns the stored level, the earned level, whether the snapshot is stale, `computed_at` and the evidence (trailing-10 rate, the PR numbers used, agent lines, owner lines by rework label), read from `dispatch/autonomy`.
2. The same endpoint returns the history from `dispatch/autonomy-history`, newest first, each with the time, the old and new level, the cause and the evidence at that moment.
3. The view renders the level and what it allows, the evidence, and the history as a list; a drop is marked in the history with its cause.
4. When the stored level is above the earned one, or the snapshot is stale, the view says so in words.
5. The endpoint never returns ticket text, a token or a key, and the surface has no route that sets the level (it stays `runner autonomy`); a test asserts a write method is refused.
6. Tests cover an empty history, a drop with its cause, a stale snapshot and a stored level above the earned one.

title: [BE] The autonomy level is earned and rolled back by the measured rewrite rate
body:
## Acceptance criteria

 1. Each merged runner PR's run row records agent lines and owner lines from git: commits by the runner's identity count as agent lines, all others as owner lines, matching the PRD's definition (owner lines over agent lines), and splits the owner lines by the `Rework: review-found` or `Rework: owner-change` line in the commit body (a commit with neither counts as `unlabelled`).
 2. `runner autonomy` shows the trailing-10 rate and, for each level, whether its advance condition holds, with the numbers.
 3. After each merged runner PR the dispatcher raises the level by one when the next level's advance condition holds and the level is 3 or below, and raises one notice naming the level and the numbers.
 4. Shadow: the advance into level 4 does not happen for the first 10 merged runner PRs after this ships; each of those PRs logs `autonomyWouldAdvance` with level 4 and the numbers. After that it advances like the others. Level 4 also requires a recorded CD flag for the target repository; level 5 needs level 4 held over 20 sampled PRs with zero reverts.
 5. The dispatcher drops the level to the highest level whose conditions hold when a rollback condition holds (a reverted auto-merged PR, a sampled rate over 10%, or any trailing-10 rate over the 20% hard ceiling) and raises one notice naming the cause.
 6. `runner autonomy -level N` stays the owner's override and refuses a level whose advance condition does not hold, with the numbers. FRG-124's blanket refusal of 4 and 5 is lifted only for a level whose condition holds.
 7. The `dispatch/autonomy` document also holds `earned` (the highest level whose advance condition holds), `evidence` (the rate, the PR numbers used, agent and owner lines, owner lines by rework label) and `computed_at`, recomputed after each merged runner PR and on `runner autonomy`; a poll reads this one document and does not recompute.
 8. A run uses the lower of `level` and `earned` (fail closed). If a recomputation fails, the snapshot is marked stale and allows no more than level 3, so a failed calculation never leaves auto-merge on.
 9. Every change of the level, up, down or by the owner, appends one document to `dispatch/autonomy-history` with the time, the old and new level, the cause and the evidence at that moment; history is never edited or deleted.
10. Tests cover the rate from fixture commits, each advance condition, the shadow count, each rollback, the 20% ceiling, a stored level above the earned one, a stale snapshot at level 4, and one history document per change.

title: [SLICE] One autonomy level replaces the auto-merge switch
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `runner autonomy` prints the current level and what it allows (for example `autonomy 0: you delegate and you merge`); `runner autonomy -level N` sets it.
2. Setting 4 or 5 is refused with the reason, naming the PRD condition, until the level's conditions are measured (FRG-126).
3. Each run records the level read when it is claimed; changing the level does not change a run already claimed.
4. pr-meta marks a PR eligible for auto-merge only when the run's recorded level is 4 or more and the existing eligibility rules hold. `run.yml` no longer reads `WINGMAN_AUTO_MERGE`, and the variable is deleted.
5. A level that is missing or cannot be read counts as 0.
6. `infra/README.md` (Pull requests and auto-merge), `docs/tech-design-v1.md` and the PRD's levels table name the setting; nothing still describes `WINGMAN_AUTO_MERGE`.

title: [BE] At autonomy 1 and above, the dispatcher delegates the next ticket itself
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. At level 1 or above, a poll delegates the next eligible ticket while today's claimed runs are below the level's bar (1, 3, 5, 5 and 10 runs a day for levels 1 to 5) and the review WIP limit has room.
2. Eligible means: open; in the earliest milestone that still has open tickets, then by priority; a `[BE]`, `[FE]` or `[SLICE]` title; a `repo:` label on the runner's allowlist and a `size:` label; no `.github/workflows/` path in its description; no settled run row (that needs `runner requeue`); no `wingman:hold` label. A ticket with an open blocker may be delegated, since the dispatcher already holds it. *Updated (2026-10-15):* the ticket's workflow state is Backlog or Todo; a ticket already started or In Review is never delegated, so the agent does not open a second build of work someone is doing.
3. At level 0 it delegates nothing.
4. Each delegation logs `ticketAutoDelegated` with the ticket, the level and the rule that chose it; a poll that delegates nothing because the bar is reached logs that once.
5. Tests cover each eligibility rule, the bar per level, level 0, and a full WIP limit.
6. *Added (2026-10-15):* a poll delegates nothing while the circuit breaker is tripped or unreadable, the default provider is halted, the default model is in its peak-price window, or the budget ceiling is reached, each logged as a skip with its reason, so the bar never paces work the dispatcher would refuse to run.

title: [SLICE] The providers view lists the plans in dispatch order with price, usage and terms verdict, read-only
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `GET /api/providers` returns each configured plan in dispatch order with its provider, price, window usage where the provider reports it ("unknown" otherwise) and recorded terms verdict.
2. The providers view renders that list and states that order and models are changed in configuration.
3. The endpoint and the view never receive, return or store an API key.
4. Negative: the surface has no route that writes a plan record, and a test asserts a write method on the endpoint is refused.
5. Tests cover the endpoint with plans in a known order, a plan whose usage is unreported, and an empty list.

title: [BE] A run records what its agent did each step, and a stalled build stops early with a named reason
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The completions record carries, per step, the tool name, the path it touched (for read, edit and write) and the request's context tokens.
2. The run summary carries files read, files edited and peak context tokens.
3. A build phase with no edit or write for DEFAULT_NO_PROGRESS_STEPS steps stops with stop reason `agent-no-progress`; its detail names the step count and peak context.
4. A later fix round resets the count; the plan stage, which never edits, is exempt.
5. Tests: a fake agent that only reads trips the guard; one that edits does not; a resumed fix round resets it.
6. Negative: a run that edits within the limit behaves exactly as today.

title: [BE] Chosen skill guidance reaches the runner's agent through the projection
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The owner names which skill guidance joins the rule stack (a short list, decided in this ticket's plan; the proposal is the per-ticket flow and the filing rules).
2. The projection generator emits that guidance for the right phase (plan, build or both), and a test shows it in the written `AGENTS.md`.
3. The prompt prefix stays byte-stable per sha (FR-19), so the cache is not broken: a test compares two builds of one sha.
4. The trimmed build projection stays within its size budget, or the ticket states the new size.
5. `--no-skills` and the isolated HOME are unchanged.

title: [BE] A run records its first-request cache share per phase, and delegations cluster to hit the cache
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The run record carries, per phase, the first request's fresh and cached input tokens and the whole-phase cached share.
2. `plan-list` or the run statistics view prints the cache share per run.
3. A note in `infra/README.md` states the observed hit rates, the likely reason the plan stage runs cold (the gap between runs against the provider's cache retention) and the batching guidance.
4. If the provider documents its cache retention, the ticket records it with the source.

title: [BE] runner plans-refresh reads each plan's vendor pages, models and leaderboard scores into dated facts
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The command writes only `provider_plans/<id>/facts/<date>`; it never calls `RecordVerdict`, `AddReply` or any opt-in write (a test with a narrow writer interface asserts nothing else is called).
2. A source that could not be read is recorded as 'could not read' with the last good read date carried forward, never as 'unchanged'.
3. Prices, limits and models come from the vendor's own page; the tokenplans feed is a change signal only; where they disagree the vendor figure is recorded with the difference noted.
4. Each model's facts carry its leaderboard score, the benchmark, the leaderboard's date, whether it was independently run or vendor-reported, and the leaderboard's stated margin.
5. A plan whose price is outside USD 10-20 is flagged in the facts document (the candidate-set removal itself is a separate dispatcher change).
6. Vendor page text is stored as quoted, size-capped data and is never treated as an instruction (a test with hostile text proves it stays inert).
7. Tests use httptest servers: success, a 500, a malformed body, and hostile text; plus the diff and the last-good carry-forward.

title: [INFRA] The build agent's container is mandatory, so the summary ready flag cannot be forged
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `runner build` and `runner plan-stage` stop with an infra-failure when `-agent-image` or `-checks-image` is empty, with a distinct stop reason that the build endings list.
2. The `model.yml` image pulls are unconditional, and the `agent-probe` workflow (canary credentials file, step files) is green on the pinned image.
3. Unit tests cover the refusal and that no agent starts on the host.
4. The README's `ready` paragraph says `ready` is advisory and steerable, and lists the gates that cover the remainder: the plan's write set, the check gates, `go` and `web`, and the pr-review verdict.
5. With `WINGMAN_TWO_STAGE=on`, one S or M dry run is recorded as evidence.

title: [BE] A blocked ticket waits until its blocker is done, not just until it stops running
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A candidate blocked by an issue whose Linear state type is anything other than `completed` or `canceled` is not admitted, and its deferral names `blocked`.
2. A candidate whose blockers are all completed or canceled is admitted as it is today.
3. The existing hold on a blocking relation with a run in flight, in either direction, is unchanged.
4. A blocker whose state cannot be read counts as open.

title: [BE] The README lists the runner's operator subcommands
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The README lists each operator subcommand in `cmd/runner/main.go` with one line saying what it does.
2. It names the variables they need (`WINGMAN_ACCOUNT`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`).
3. It says which are safe to run read-only (the ones with a dry-run flag or that only read).
4. No code or workflow changes.

title: [BE] A priority edit reaches a queued run within one poll
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A queued or planned run's stored rank follows its ticket's Linear priority within one poll.
2. A run that is claimed, waiting or settled keeps its rank.
3. A poll in which the rank is unchanged writes nothing to that row.
4. A failed refresh is logged and the poll still admits.

title: [BE] The READMEs document the agent container and egress switches
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The README or the infra README names both variables, what each switches, and that egress needs the image set.
2. It states the undo for each.
3. It names `agent-probe` as the way to prove the container and its egress.
4. No code or workflow changes.

title: [BE] Ledger reservations are keyed by attempt
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A `Settle` for attempt k leaves attempt k+1's reservation in place.
2. `TryClaim`, `Settle`, `Release`, `Requeue`, `Suspend` and the sweep use the same attempt-aware key.
3. A claim in flight at deploy, holding the old key, still settles.

title: [BE] The queue stops reading rows that lack queued_at
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. After a backfill with `skipped` at 0, `Candidates` issues one ordered query.
2. A queued row that still lacks `queued_at` is logged, not silently dropped.
3. The ordering tests pass without the legacy-row cases.

title: [INFRA] The agent-probe credentials job can authenticate
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. ~~Dispatching ~~`~~agent-probe~~`~~ from ~~`~~main~~`~~ passes its auth step.~~ **Updated (2026-10-13):** the credentials job runs and passes from `main` and from a branch; the cloud auth step was replaced by a canary credentials file (see the plan comment on this ticket).
2. The proof still shows the container cannot read the credentials file or write the step's files.
3. The egress job is unaffected.

title: [BE] A run whose runner died stops holding a slot and can be redriven
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A claim with no outcome past the runner's hard timeout plus a margin is marked abandoned with a reason.
2. An abandoned run no longer counts toward the budget reservation or the WIP limit.
3. Each abandonment raises one error-tracker issue naming the run and ticket.
4. `runner requeue` returns an abandoned run to the queue.
5. A claim younger than that window is never abandoned, even when its runner is slow.
6. An abandoned run is never requeued automatically.

title: [BE] An urgent ticket starts within seconds of being prioritised
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Two queued runs of equal priority are claimed oldest-queued first.
2. A higher-priority run is claimed before any lower-priority one, whatever its queue age.
3. Raising a queued ticket's priority in Linear starts a poll within a minute, with no scheduler tick.
4. A Linear edit to anything other than priority, or to an issue not in the queue, starts no poll.
5. With webhooks lost, the 15-min scheduled poll still admits and claims runs as today.

title: [BE] Front-end PRs wait for the owner, whatever their size
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. An S or M PR whose changed files match the repo's front-end paths is not marked for auto-merge.
2. An S or M PR whose ticket carries the front-end label is not marked for auto-merge, whatever it changed.
3. An S or M PR matching neither is marked for auto-merge exactly as today.
4. Each repo in the allowlist can declare its own front-end paths; a repo declaring none holds nothing on paths.
5. The PR states why it waits for the owner.

title: [INFRA] The bun version agrees across model.yml, plan-smoke.yml and the agent image
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A check compares ~~the three pins~~ every pin of the bun omp runs on: each workflow that installs omp, and `tools/agent/Dockerfile`.
2. Changing one makes it fail, and the failure names ~~the three files~~ every pinned file with its version.
3. It passes on the current pins.

Updated (2026-11-03): criteria 1 and 2 now cover every place omp runs. Since this ticket was written, `review-smoke.yml` and `pr-review.yml` also install omp on the host with their own bun pin, so checking only three files would leave two to drift; the check finds omp-installing workflows itself, so a new one is covered without editing it.

title: [BE] The agent and checks containers share one set of hardening flags
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A flag added in that one place appears in both containers' docker commands.
2. The checks container's behaviour and tests are unchanged.
3. The agent container's tests still kill each guard when it is mutated.

title: [BE] The PR-review and smoke agents run in the agent container
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Each of the three runs its agent in the container when the variable is set.
2. With it unset they run as they do today.
3. A probe shows none of them can read the credentials file or append to a step file.

title: [BE] The agent-container probe mirrors a real run
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Both versions are checked in the container as a real run runs them.
2. An image missing either binary stops the run at agent-start with stop reason `agent-container`.
3. The start-up time is still recorded per run.

title: [BE] A run with no recorded plan is never auto-merge-eligible
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A run with no recorded plan is not labelled eligible, whatever its size, review result or check results.
2. The PR body or a status comment states that the run was held back for having no recorded plan.
3. A run with a recorded plan whose write set stays inside it is labelled exactly as today.
4. `infra/README.md`'s paragraph naming this gap is updated to say what now holds.

title: [INFRA] The agent's container image is built, published and pinned by digest
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A Dockerfile builds an image with bun and node from base images pinned by digest, omp and opencode installed from the tools/omp and tools/opencode lockfiles, and git.
2. A workflow publishes it when the Dockerfile or either lockfile changes and reports the digest.
3. The published image's omp --version and opencode --version match the lockfile versions.
4. The model job can pull it without a credential that job does not already hold.
5. WINGMAN_AGENT_IMAGE is set to the digest and FRG-75's agent-probe passes against it.

title: [BE] The agent container can reach only its model API
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. From the agent container a request to the model API host succeeds.
2. A request to any other host, and to the metadata address, fails.
3. Both harnesses (omp and opencode) complete a build with the restriction on.
4. A run that times out or is cancelled leaves no proxy or network behind.
5. With no allowlist configured, behaviour matches the plain container run (negative).

title: [BE] The README says how to switch between off-peak-only and always
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The README states that, by default, a run is not started while its model's peak-price window is open or would be reached before it finishes, and that the windows come from the model's rate in `providers.json`.
2. The README names the two modes, `off-peak-only` and `always`.
3. The README gives the commands to read and to set the mode, with the environment variables they need.
4. No file other than README.md changes.

title: [BE] Development runs wait out their model's peak-price hours
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. In off-peak-only mode, the default, a queued run is not claimed while the peak window of the model it would run on is open, or would be reached before its estimated finish, for its plan stage and its build stage alike, and its row records that it is waiting on peak hours.
2. The same run is claimed at the first poll after the window closes.
3. In always mode a run is claimed during the window exactly as today.
4. The owner can switch between the two modes without a redeploy, and the switch takes effect at the next poll.
5. A run on a model with no peak pricing, and a run on a free tier, is never held in either mode.
6. A run held for peak hours is not moved to another plan or a free tier and raises no notice: it waits (negative).

title: [FE] The surface shows the peak window and switches runs between off-peak only and always
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. For each model a run may use, the surface shows whether it has peak pricing and, if so, its window; a flat-priced model is shown as such.
2. The mode control is offered only when at least one configured model has peak pricing, and it shows the current mode and whether admission is holding runs now.
3. Switching the mode in the surface takes effect at the next poll.
4. The mode survives a dispatcher restart, and only the owner can change it (the surface's existing IAP boundary).

title: [BE] The README says how to run the store tests against the Firestore emulator
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The Checks section states that the store and record tests need `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` and skip without it.
2. The Checks section gives the command that starts the emulator the way CI does, and the environment variable to set.
3. Running the section's two commands in order on a clean checkout runs the store tests rather than skipping them.
4. No file other than README.md changes.

title: [FE] The providers view shows the plan order and sets each plan's plan, build and review model
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. The view lists the configured plans in dispatch order, with each plan's provider, price, window usage where the provider reports it ("unknown" otherwise) and recorded terms verdict.
2. Reordering the plans changes which plan the next dispatched ticket starts on; a run already in flight keeps its plan.
3. Under each plan the owner can set the plan, build and review model, and the next dispatch on that plan uses them.
4. A setting that breaks a rule the runner enforces, such as a review model equal to the build model, is refused with the reason shown.
5. The view never receives, shows or stores an API key; adding a new plan stays a configuration step outside the surface.
6. Negative: with no edits made, dispatch uses the configured defaults exactly as today.

title: [BE] A plan stage that fails holds its reservation and wedges dispatch
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* A plan stage that writes no artifact ends the run with a recorded stop naming the plan, and releases what it holds.
* No regression for the happy path, and a genuinely long-running plan is not preempted.

title: [BE] A run whose PR rebase conflicts is discarded with no re-plan
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* A run whose pr job hits a rebase conflict is re-planned or re-applied against the new base, and ends in a PR or a recorded business outcome, not an infra-failure.
* No regression for a genuinely unresolvable diff, which must still fail loudly.

title: [BE] Retire the runner's own out-of-plan claim and model.yml's unread ready output
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. `Summary.OutOfPlanFiles` is gone from the summary, the record and the parse/cap paths — the audit trail it was keeping is superseded by the trusted write set pr-meta computes and the run record already carries.
2. `model.yml` no longer declares a `ready` job or workflow output, and `BuildResult.Ready` goes with it, leaving no orphan.
3. The pre-PR loop's own readiness decision is unaffected: `sum.Ready` still drives the summary, the record and pr-meta's draft decision.
4. `make check` green.

title: [BE] A ticket whose run stopped can be dispatched again
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Given a run whose outcome is a stop, when the owner asks for that ticket to be retried, then the dispatcher admits it again on a later poll.
2. Given a ticket already attempted, when no retry has been asked for, then every poll leaves it alone, so a stop is never retried in a loop.
3. A retry is recorded: the run record or the ledger states that this attempt is a retry, and of which attempt.
4. The mechanism is an operator action, never automatic.

title: [BE] A build on the free tier falls through the free-model list
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. On a free-tier run, a build model that is withdrawn or unavailable falls to the next model in the plan's free list, in order; when none answer, the run stops as today.
2. The review never runs on the model that built this run: on the free tier it uses the first free model, in list order, that did not build. If none is left, the run has no review and its PR opens as a draft.
3. Paid runs behave exactly as today, including their review list.

title: [BE] The build agent runs where it cannot reach the job's credentials or step outputs
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A probe run as the agent cannot read the GCP credentials file the auth step wrote.
2. A probe run as the agent cannot change any of the job's step outputs, environment or summary files; the build job's outputs match what the runner wrote.
3. The agent still reaches its model API, and a build on the default model succeeds end to end.
4. A run that times out or is cancelled leaves no agent process or container behind.
5. The agent's added start-up time is recorded per run, and the run stays within NFR-1's 60 minutes.
6. With no container image configured, runs behave exactly as today, so local runs and tests need no Docker.

title: [BE] A review-smoke job shows which free model can review a PR
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. A manually dispatched `review-smoke` workflow runs the review prompt on a fixture diff with each model in its input list, under the restricted review profile.
2. A model passes when the review-findings block parses and the run costs $0; the job summary lists each model's result.
3. It edits nothing and holds no GitHub write token.
4. It follows `plan-smoke`'s shape (`internal/runner/plan_smoke.go`, `.github/workflows/plan-smoke.yml`).

title: [BE] An S or M PR the review gate passes merges automatically (FR-16)
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. An S or M PR opened ready with zero open boxes and not selected into the 20% sample requests auto-merge, and merges once its required checks pass.
2. An L PR, a sampled PR, and any PR flagged for owner attention never request auto-merge (negative).
3. A push after auto-merge was requested withdraws it, and the PR comes back to the owner (FR-16).
4. Auto-merge conditions live in branch protection, not in the runner's own judgment.

title: [SLICE] A run asks for the decisions it may not take alone in its Linear agent session and waits for the answer (guided mode)
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Only an outward, irreversible, security or scope decision is posted; a local, evidenced choice that grants nothing never is (negative).
2. A posted decision is one `elicitation` with `signal: select`: at most 4 options, the recommended first, each with its cost, at most 3 lines of context.
3. A decision raised at the plan stage pauses the run holding no runner and no reservation, and a `prompted` reply resumes it with the answer recorded on its run record.
4. Free text matching no option is answered with the same options again, never guessed.
5. No reply within a configured time (default 24 h) stops the run as waiting-on-owner with one Slack notice.
6. The PRD gains an owner-escalation requirement, separate from FR-13.

title: [BE] A run records which harness ran each step
body:
**Acceptance criteria**

* **Given** a run routed to a plan's default harness, **when** its record is read, **then** each step names that harness.
* **Given** the default is not ready and the fallback runs, **then** the steps name the fallback.
* **Given** a phase starts, **then** one log line names its harness and model.

title: [BE] The review phase falls back to a second vendor and logs why an agent run failed
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* The review's default availability order has a second model from a different vendor than the first and than the build model: Laguna S 2.1 (free on GOAT). It is set once in models.json, and run.yml's default matches it.
* An agent run that fails logs the tail of its error output with the stop reason, so a `model-unavailable` can be traced to its cause from the run log.
* A review whose first model fails with a server error is completed by the second.

title: [BE] A free-model plan is the last fallback when every paid plan is out of allowance
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* `providers.json` can mark a plan as last resort, with an ordered list of free models. OpenCode Zen (`https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`) is the first such plan, keyed by a named secret.
* When every paid plan refuses on allowance, the dispatcher admits the run on the last-resort plan instead of stopping. The run record names the plan.
* A withdrawn free model (unknown or unavailable) falls to the next one. When none answer, the run stops as today.
* A private repo uses the last-resort plan only when opted in.
* The harness reaches each free model through the API it needs (chat completions or responses), proven by a live fixture.
* The free models and their order are chosen by measurement on the harness A/B task and recorded with the date.

title: [BE] opencode is the fallback harness
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* An opencode adapter (one file) passes the conformance suite from FRG-57, with fixtures recorded live (`normal`, `readonly`, `badkey`), including a live proof that its read-only profile refuses edit, write and shell.
* `TestNoRetiredHarnessIsNamed` (added when opencode was retired) is removed or narrowed, since opencode is a supported harness again.
* opencode's cost is priced from its token usage and the plan's rates (it reports 0 for a custom provider).
* CI installs opencode pinned beside omp; the GOAT plan's fallback harness is opencode.
* The Command Code CLI's runner adapter is removed once this adapter passes the suite.

title: [BE] A coding plan is a configuration entry, not a code path
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* Each plan in `internal/providers/providers.json` carries its OpenAI-compatible base URL, the NAME of the secret holding its key, its windows, its per-model monthly caps, and the harnesses allowed on it.
* GOAT's entry keeps its plan-wide windows ($14 five-hour, $35 weekly, $70 monthly) and adds a per-model monthly cap map (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $60; other models as the plan lists them). A run is admitted only while both its model's cap and the plan's windows have room.
* Adding a second plan is a config entry, a secret and a `runner plan-define` record, proven by a test that adds a fake plan with no Go change.
* A model whose prefix has no plan entry is refused at dispatch, as today.
* Existing GOAT runs behave as today.

title: [BE] omp is the default harness
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* An omp adapter (one file) passes the conformance suite from FRG-57, with fixtures recorded live (`normal`, `readonly`, `badkey`), including a probe that the read-only profile refuses creating a new file.
* CI installs omp pinned, with bun, in `model.yml` and `plan-smoke.yml`.
* The GOAT plan's default harness is omp on its built-in `commandcode` provider; its fallback is opencode once FRG-65 lands, and the Command Code CLI until then.
* omp's cost is priced from its token usage and the plan's rates: `providers.json` gains GOAT's `rates` (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash off-peak $0.15 / $0.60 / $0.003 per M, doubled 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC on weekdays), with time-of-use pricing the rate card can express. omp's own figure was wrong in both directions.
* A live run on main builds through omp and reaches a PR.

title: [BE] A run whose base predates a workflow change on main still pushes
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* The pr job rebases the run's commits onto current main before pushing.
* A rebase conflict stops the run with a named stop reason, and the bundle stays available.
* Runs on a current base behave as today.

title: [BE] A run that would edit .github/workflows stops before it spends
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* An M or L run whose plan names any path under `.github/workflows/` stops at the plan phase with stop reason `workflow-change`, before the build agent runs.
* A run whose build edits a path under `.github/workflows/` anyway (an S ticket, or an edit outside the plan) records `workflow-change` and does not attempt the push; the bundle stays available as today.
* The run record and logs name the workflow files involved.
* The README's hand-over section says tickets that change workflows are built and pushed by hand.
* Runs that touch no workflow file behave as today.

title: [BE] A ticket whose text matches a masked value reaches the build empty
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* A ticket whose text contains a value masked in the ticket job still reaches the build intact.
* No job output carries ticket text.
* An empty or missing ticket stops the run with a reason naming the hand-off, not `ticket-missing`.
* Runs for ordinary tickets behave as today.

title: [BE] A review fix round's PR says which findings it addressed
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* When the run-duration budget allows, the review runs once more on the diff after the fix round, and the PR lists only the findings still open.
* When the budget does not allow it, the PR labels the list 'addressed by a fix round, not re-reviewed' instead of 'open'.
* A clean re-review with passing checks opens the PR as ready.
* A run with no review findings behaves as today.

title: [BE] No provider or plan is named in Go logic
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. No provider or plan is named in the runner's or dispatcher's non-test Go source: model identifiers, billing windows, ceilings and availability-error patterns are read from provider configuration.
2. Adding or replacing a provider is a configuration change only.
3. A search of non-test Go source for any configured vendor's name finds nothing.

title: [BE] Harnesses are adapters chosen by configuration and proven by one conformance suite
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* One shared contract suite runs against every adapter: prompt on stdin; a read-only profile refuses edit, write and shell (FR-3); resume keeps one session across rounds (FR-28); events translate to the runner's shape with token usage; cost comes from tokens times the plan's rates when the harness's own figure is absent or wrong; bad-key and limit exits classify correctly; the credential is deleted after each attempt (FR-11).
* The Command Code adapter passes the suite.
* Harness choice is read from configuration (default plus ordered fallback per plan).
* An adapter that fails the suite cannot be selected.

title: [BE] Cost drift is flagged, and the comparison shows real-run pass rate and cost
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. When a run's cost per ticket is more than 25% above that provider's own trailing average, the run summary shows a flag, and dispatch continues unaffected.
2. Once a provider is in use, the comparison shows each model's measured pass rate and cost per ticket from real runs, with no separate evaluation spend.
3. Where a provider prices by the hour, each run's cost is tagged peak or off-peak, so time-of-use spend can be summed.

title: [BE] A build that edits outside its plan opens a flagged draft PR instead of stopping
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* A build with files outside its plan still commits, pushes and opens its PR, as a draft.
* The PR body states "edited outside the plan:" with the file list, and the run record keeps the list.
* A build inside its plan behaves as today.
* PRD FR-4 says out-of-plan edits draft the PR rather than stop the run.

title: [BE] A run's first model request hits the prompt cache across runs
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* A second run within the provider's cache window reads at least 90% of request 1 from cache.
* A run's build phase reads at least 95% from cache from the second run onward, measured from the `modelRequest` lines.
* Review and fix rounds behave as today; existing tests stay green.

title: [BE] The runner writes commits and PRs in the repo's conventional style
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* The build agent ends with a fenced block carrying a conventional subject, bullet body and summary; the runner validates the subject (conventional form, contains the ticket id) and uses it for the commit, the PR title and the PR Summary.
* When the block is missing or invalid, the runner falls back to a deterministic subject: type from the lane or Bug label, scope from the changed files' top package, lowercase summary.
* Tests cover a valid block, an invalid one, and a missing one.

title: [BE] README documents the model labels a ticket can carry
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* The README's label table gains a row per model label, with its value format and what it overrides.
* It states that a review model equal to the build model is refused.

title: [BE] Review ≠ build also checks the build's fallback models
body:
## Acceptance criteria

* Build stops with `StopModelInvalid` when a review model equals the build model or any of its fallbacks.
* A test covers a review list that names a build fallback.

title: [BE] Every ready PR gets an automatic model review, on a free model now and a paid one by configuration later
body:
**Acceptance criteria**

1. Given a PR marked ready for review, when the workflow runs, then it posts one review comment of findings from a model checking the diff against the linked ticket's ACs, in the review-findings contract the runner already parses.
2. Given a draft PR, or a push after the review, when events fire, then no review runs.
3. Given the model setting, when it names a free model that passed the FRG-37 review/plan probe, then that model reviews; changing it to a paid model is a one-line configuration edit, no code change.
4. Given the reviewer, when it runs, then it cannot edit files or run commands, its token can only write PR comments, and the PR text and diff are treated as data.
5. Given the model is unavailable or refused, when the review runs, then it tries the next configured model and, if all fail, the `wingman-review` status is a failure, the comment says "no verdict", and the PR is not auto-merged; it waits for the owner. Manual merge is never blocked.
6. Given a free model, when a review runs, then cash spend is zero and the model used is recorded.
7. Given the repository, when make check runs, then it passes.
8. Given a ready PR, when its review is clean, the PR is marked eligible and its head has not moved since the review, then the review requests auto-merge; nothing else requests it.

title: [BE] README explains how to hand Forge Wingman a ticket
body:
**Acceptance criteria**

1. Given the README, when read, then it has a 'Use' section that says a ticket is handed over by delegating it to the Forge Wingman app in Linear.
2. Given the same section, when read, then it names the two labels a ticket needs, a size label and a repo label, in the form the dispatcher actually accepts.
3. Given the same section, when read, then it says how often the dispatcher looks for new tickets.
4. Given the change, when reviewed, then no file other than README.md is modified.
5. Given the repository, when make check runs, then it passes.

title: [BE] README links to the deploy docs
body:
**Acceptance criteria**

1. Given the README, when read, then it has a "Deploy" section that links to `infra/README.md`.
2. Given the change, when reviewed, then no file other than `README.md` is modified.
3. Given the repository, when `make check` runs, then it passes.

title: [BE] Dispatcher gets a fresh Linear token each poll instead of a pasted one
body:
**Acceptance criteria**

1. Given the app's client id and secret in Secret Manager, when a poll starts, then it obtains a token for that poll and uses it only there.
2. Given Linear answers a request with 401, when a poll is running, then it gets one new token and retries once, and a second 401 ends the poll with a logged failure that admits nothing.
3. Given the token exchange itself fails, when a poll runs, then it fails loudly and admits nothing, rather than polling with a stale token.
4. Given Secret Manager after this ships, when listed, then no access token is stored anywhere, only the client id and client secret.
5. Given a poll, when it calls Linear, then the header is `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

title: [SLICE] An M or L run plans before it is admitted, so runs with disjoint write sets share a repository
body:
## Acceptance criteria

 1. An M or L run is admitted to build only after its plan exists and its file list is recorded on its run record.
 2. The plan stage checks and books its own budget reservation, under the same ceilings as a build, before it starts; a plan the budget can't yet afford waits, and the binding condition is recorded.
 3. The plan stage keeps `edit` and `bash` denied (FR-3), and a failed or empty plan ends the run as a failed run does today, with no build.
 4. Two M or L runs in the same repository whose planned file lists are disjoint are admitted together, up to the concurrency limit N.
 5. Two M or L runs in the same repository whose planned file lists overlap are not admitted together; the later one waits and records why.
 6. Across overlapping polls, the reserved total across the plan and build stages never exceeds the budget ceiling.
 7. The one-run-per-repository interim rule no longer blocks M or L runs with known, disjoint plans, and still applies to any run whose write set is unknown.
 8. A build that edits a file outside its plan's list still opens its PR as a draft listing those files, exactly as today (negative).
 9. A run held up by contention at the plan stage is an infrastructure outcome and never triggers escalation.
10. The PRD states when the plan's file list becomes known and that admission uses it.
11. Auto-merge eligibility comes from a trusted plan file list: `pr-meta` computes out-of-plan from the bundle's plan files against the PR's changed files and feeds `ownerAttention`, so the model job's `out_of_plan_files` output cannot make an out-of-plan PR eligible.

title: Isolate pre-PR check execution from the model job's secrets
body:
## Acceptance criteria

1. Given a build round produces changes, when the checks run, then each gate runs in a container started with `--network none` whose only mounts are the worktree, a read-only module cache, a throwaway build cache, the host's pinned `golangci-lint` binary and the repository's git common dir, so neither a GCP credential file nor the network is reachable from the checks' process.
2. Given a check fails, when the result must reach the model job's retry loop, then the failing gate name and its output reach back within one round-trip, without exposing the model job's environment to the checked-out branch code.
3. Given the container round-trip, when up to 3 rounds run, then each round's duration is recorded (the `checkRound` `durationMS` log line and the run record's `checks` duration) and the loop stays within NFR-1's 60-minute cap.
4. Given this ships, then `internal/runner/checks.go`'s comment describes the container boundary instead of saying the full fix is tracked separately.

title: [SLICE] The webhook wakes the dispatcher
body:
**Acceptance criteria**

* **Given** a delegation, **when** Linear sends the `AgentSessionEvent`, **then** a
  dispatcher execution starts within seconds (`adr/0013`).
* **Given** a body whose `Linear-Signature` does not verify, **when** received, **then**
  it is rejected and nothing is written.
* **Given** the same ticket from the webhook and the poll, **when** both arrive, **then**
  one run record exists.
* **Given** the service, **when** provisioned, **then** it is OpenTofu, and it decides
  nothing beyond enqueue-and-wake.

title: [SLICE] The systemic-failure notice
body:
**Acceptance criteria**

* **Given** a stop of class FR-11, FR-12, NFR-1 allowance exhausted, or FR-26
  infrastructure, **when** recorded, **then** one link-only notice is posted (FR-23).
* **Given** an FR-22 deferral, **when** its binding ceiling will not clear before the
  next poll, **then** it notifies; otherwise it stays silent (FR-23).
* **Given** any other stop, **when** recorded, **then** nothing is posted.
* **Given** a notice, **when** read, **then** it carries the class and a link, and no
  completion text or ticket body.
* **Given** a stop of a notify class other than FR-26's infrastructure stop, **when** recorded, **then** it trips FR-27's circuit
  breaker: no further run is admitted until a manual reset. ~~Given a stop of a notify class~~
